items.Requirement: Copilot-eligible base plan held by every licensed user
items.Rationale: The original requirement recognised only Microsoft 365 E3/E5 and Business Premium. Microsoft has since considerably widened the list of base subscriptions that are eligible for the Copilot add-on: Microsoft 365 E3/E5/E7, F1/F3, A1/A3/A5, Business and Apps, but also Office 365 E1/E1 Plus/E3/E5/F3, the Teams plans (Essentials, Enterprise, EEA, Rooms), Exchange Kiosk/Plan 1/Plan 2, SharePoint and OneDrive Plan 1/2, Planner and Project, Visio and Clipchamp. Too narrow a filter produces a false blocking verdict on an Office 365 E3 or Teams-only tenant that is perfectly eligible, and delays a viable deployment on the strength of a mistaken diagnosis. Conversely, reasoning at tenant level without checking that every holder of a Copilot licence also holds a base plan lets seats at around USD 30 per month through: they are billed and completely inoperative, because Copilot then has no Office application and no Microsoft 365 service to build on. The check therefore cross-references, user by user, the licences assigned against the official list of base plans.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Billing > Your products
3. Note the base subscriptions held (Microsoft 365, Office 365, Teams, Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Project, Visio, Clipchamp)
4. Left-hand menu: Billing > Licences > click Microsoft 365 Copilot
5. 'Assigned users' tab: for each user, open their record > Licences and apps
6. Check that an eligible base plan is ticked there as well
7. Any Copilot user without a base plan must either be given a base licence or hand back their Copilot seat
items.Expected: Every holder of a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence holds at least one eligible base plan: Microsoft 365 E3/E5/E7/F1/F3/A1/A3/A5, Business Basic/Standard/Premium, Apps for business/for enterprise; Office 365 E1/E1 Plus/E3/E5/F3/A1/A3/A5; Teams Essentials/Enterprise/EEA/Rooms; Exchange Kiosk/Plan 1/Plan 2; SharePoint Kiosk/Plan 1/Plan 2; OneDrive Plan 1/Plan 2; Planner Plan 1, Project Plan 3/5, Project Online Essentials; Visio Plan 1/Plan 2; Clipchamp. In government environments: Microsoft 365 G3/G5/F1 and Office 365 G1/G3/G5/F3. Expected outcome: 0 Copilot-licensed users without an eligible base plan.
items.Verification: $skus = Get-MgSubscribedSku -All; $copilot = @($skus | Where-Object { $_.SkuPartNumber -like '*COPILOT*' }).SkuId; Get-MgUser -All -Property userPrincipalName,assignedLicenses | Where-Object { $_.AssignedLicenses.SkuId | Where-Object { $_ -in $copilot } } | Where-Object { -not (@($_.AssignedLicenses.SkuId | ForEach-Object { ($skus | Where-Object SkuId -eq $_).SkuPartNumber }) | Where-Object { $_ -in $eligibleBasePlans }) } | Select-Object UserPrincipalName

items.Requirement: Microsoft 365 Copilot SKU purchased and visible on the tenant
items.Rationale: The Microsoft 365 Copilot SKU is a separate subscription (around USD 30 per user per month) that is not included in any base licence, not even E5. Until this subscription has been purchased and is visible on the tenant, it is impossible to assign the Copilot licence to any user whatsoever. Without this step, the whole of the rest of the checklist is inapplicable, because the Copilot service simply does not exist in the environment.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Billing > Purchase services
3. Search for 'Microsoft 365 Copilot'
4. Buy the number of licences required
5. After purchase: Billing > Licences > check that 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' appears in the list
items.Expected: Microsoft_365_Copilot SKU present with available units > 0
items.Verification: Get-MgSubscribedSku | Where {$_.SkuPartNumber -like '*COPILOT*'} | Select SkuPartNumber, @{N='Available';E={$_.PrepaidUnits.Enabled - $_.ConsumedUnits}}

items.Requirement: Copilot licence assigned and Copilot service plan genuinely provisioned
items.Rationale: Listing the SkuPartNumber that has been assigned proves nothing on its own: a Copilot licence can be assigned while its service plan is turned off, either through the disabledPlans set at assignment time (a frequent outcome of group-based assignment with an inherited licence template), or by clearing the app under 'Licences and apps' in the admin centre. The plan may equally remain at provisioningStatus 'PendingProvisioning' for several hours after assignment while it propagates. In every one of these cases the user consumes a billed seat but sees no Copilot button at all: Microsoft explicitly documents the disabled service plan and propagation in progress as the main causes of the 'Copilot is missing from the ribbon' symptom. Checking the SKU without checking the state of the service plan produces a misleading green just before go-live, and it is the leading cause of 'I have the licence but no Copilot' tickets.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Users > Active users > select a target user
3. Licences and apps tab
4. Check that 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' is ticked AND expand the Apps section
5. Check that no Copilot app has been cleared there (cleared plans populate disabledPlans)
--- Group-based assignment ---
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Groups > select the Copilot group > Licences
3. Open the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence template and check that no service plan is turned off in it
--- Propagation ---
A plan still being provisioned (PendingProvisioning) resolves on its own: re-check after 24 to 48 hours before treating it as a gap.
items.Expected: For every target user: the Copilot SKU is present, none of their Copilot service plans appears in assignedLicenses[].disabledPlans, and servicePlans[].provisioningStatus is 'Success' for all Copilot plans. Any user at 'PendingProvisioning' is reported as propagation in progress, to be re-checked after 24 to 48 hours, and not as compliant.
items.Verification: (Get-MgUserLicenseDetail -UserId 'user@domain.com').ServicePlans | Where-Object { $_.ServicePlanName -like '*COPILOT*' } | Select-Object ServicePlanName, ProvisioningStatus

items.Requirement: Licences assigned through an Entra ID group (not manually)
items.Rationale: Manual licence assignment is a source of errors and delays: a new employee may wait days before receiving their Copilot licence, and departures are not always followed by removal of the licence. An Entra ID security group fully automates the lifecycle: adding a member to the group assigns the licence instantly, and removing them releases it. Without this automation the risk is twofold: eligible users deprived of Copilot, and licences at USD 30 per month wasted on inactive accounts.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Groups > All groups > New group
3. Name: GRP-Copilot-Users, Type: Security
4. Add the target members
5. Click the group > Licences > Assign
6. Tick Microsoft 365 Copilot > Save
items.Expected: GRP-Copilot-Users group with the Copilot licence assigned to the group
items.Verification: Get-MgGroup -Filter "displayName eq 'GRP-Copilot-Users'"

items.Requirement: Check that the Copilot subscription does not expire within 60 days
items.Rationale: A Copilot subscription that is not renewed causes the immediate loss of the service for all the users concerned on the expiry date, with no warning inside the Office applications. Users lose access to the Copilot button, to Teams summaries and to Copilot Chat overnight. Checking that automatic renewal is turned on and that expiry is more than 60 days away avoids this abrupt interruption and gives the purchasing team time to handle the renewal calmly.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Billing > Your products
3. Locate 'Microsoft 365 Copilot'
4. Check the expiry date and the renewal status
5. If renewal is turned off: click the product > Edit renewal settings > turn it on
items.Expected: Auto-renewal = Yes, expiry > 60 days away
items.Verification: Get-MgSubscribedSku | Where {$_.SkuPartNumber -like '*COPILOT*'}

items.Requirement: Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise deployed on the workstations
items.Rationale: Copilot integrates directly into the ribbon of the Office applications as a button and a side pane, but that integration exists only in Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise, the subscription version updated monthly. Perpetual versions (Office 2016, 2019 or 2021) never receive the feature updates that include Copilot. A user with perpetual Office will have their Copilot licence consumed but will never see the Copilot button in Word, Excel or PowerPoint. Without migration to M365 Apps, the Copilot investment is wasted on those workstations.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://config.office.com
2. Left-hand menu: Inventory
3. Review the list of devices and the 'Office Version' column
4. Identify the workstations running perpetual Office (2016/2019/2021) versus M365 Apps
5. If perpetual Office is detected: plan the migration through Intune or the ODT
--- Local check on a workstation ---
1. Open Word > File > Account
2. Check that the product displayed is 'Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise' (not 'Office 2019' or '2021')
items.Expected: Product = Microsoft 365 Apps (not Office 2019/2021)
items.Verification: Check locally: Word > File > Account

items.Requirement: Update channel = Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise
items.Rationale: Microsoft rolls new Copilot features out to Current Channel first, then to Monthly Enterprise Channel, and finally to Semi-Annual Channel with a delay of four to six months. Staying on the Semi-Annual channel means that users have no access to the latest Copilot capabilities (new prompt types, quality improvements, new features in Excel or PowerPoint) for months after their release. Without the right update channel, the organisation is paying for a Copilot service of which it receives only a degraded and outdated version.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://config.office.com
2. Left-hand menu: Cloud Update
3. Check the channels displayed: Monthly Enterprise Channel, Current Channel
4. If devices are on Semi-Annual: click 'Enable cloud update' to switch them over
5. Or: left-hand menu Customization > Device Configuration
6. Create/edit a profile > Update channel > 'Current Channel' or 'Monthly Enterprise'
7. Assign the profile to the target devices
--- Alternative through Intune ---
1. Open https://intune.microsoft.com
2. Devices > Configuration > Create > Administrative templates
3. Search for 'Update Channel' > select Current Channel
4. Assign to the target device group
items.Expected: Channel = Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel
items.Verification: Local registry: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Office\ClickToRun\Configuration\CDNBaseUrl

items.Requirement: Modern Authentication (OAuth2) enabled on the tenant
items.Rationale: Copilot uses OAuth2 (modern authentication) exclusively to authenticate against the Microsoft 365 services and to reach the user's data through Microsoft Graph. Basic authentication (Basic Auth), which is obsolete and less secure, does not support the tokens Copilot needs in order to operate. If modern authentication is disabled on the Exchange tenant, Copilot cannot authenticate and the Copilot features in Outlook (summaries, drafts, coaching) are completely inoperative. Microsoft is progressively deprecating Basic Auth; enabling it also constitutes a major security risk.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Settings > Org settings
3. 'Services' tab > 'Modern authentication'
4. Check that 'Enable modern authentication for Outlook 2013 and later versions' is ticked
5. If it is disabled: tick it and save
--- Note ---
Modern Auth has been enabled by default since 2017. Basic Auth was permanently disabled in 2023.
If this option is unticked, it has been deliberately changed.
items.Expected: OAuth2ClientProfileEnabled = True
items.Verification: Get-OrganizationConfig | Select OAuth2ClientProfileEnabled

items.Requirement: Connected experiences enabled
items.Expected: All 3 connected experiences policy settings set to Enabled (registry value 1). Read from Intune first when the policy is delivered there, otherwise from a reference workstation.
items.Verification: Intune: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies?$expand=settings (DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All); workstation: HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy and HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Cloud\Office\16.0\common\privacy (1 = Enabled, 2 = Disabled)
items.Rationale: Connected experiences are the technical channel through which the Office applications communicate with Microsoft's cloud services, including Copilot. They allow Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook to send user requests to the Copilot service and to receive the responses generated by the AI. If this option is disabled through a group policy or a privacy policy, the Copilot button disappears entirely from the ribbon of every Office application. Without this configuration, Copilot is completely invisible and inaccessible, even for a correctly licensed user. Documented limitation, stated plainly: the Cloud Policy service (config.office.com) exposes no public API that would allow these three policy settings to be read back; only five Copilot settings have a Graph bridge (the copilotPolicySetting resource), and connected experiences are not among them. The state can therefore only be read automatically when the organisation delivers the policy through Intune (settings catalog or ingested Office ADMX); failing that, the requirement legitimately remains a workstation check. Two details that matter for diagnosis: policy settings delivered by Cloud Policy are written under HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Cloud\Office\16.0 and take precedence over Group Policy; the registry values are 1 = Enabled and 2 = Disabled, not 0 or 1.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://config.office.com
2. On the home page: click the 'Office policies' card
   (or left-hand menu: Customization > Policy management)
3. Click 'Create' to create a new policy
4. Name: 'Copilot-ConnectedExperiences'
5. Scope: select the Copilot security group
6. In the list of policies, search for 'connected'
7. Set these 3 policies to 'Enabled':
   - Allow the use of connected experiences in Office
   - Allow the use of connected experiences that analyze content
   - Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office
8. Save and publish the policy
--- Alternative through GPO ---
User Configuration > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center
--- Alternative through Intune (settings catalog) ---
Intune > Devices > Configuration > Create > Settings catalog > Microsoft Office > Privacy:
set the 3 policy settings to Enabled. This is the only path that can be read back through an API
(GET /beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies?$expand=settings).
--- Registry values ---
disconnectedstate, usercontentdisabled, downloadcontentdisabled, controllerconnectedservicesenabled:
1 = Enabled, 2 = Disabled

items.Requirement: MFA enabled for all Copilot users through Conditional Access
items.Rationale: Copilot considerably amplifies the risk posed by a compromised account: an attacker can use Copilot to query all of the victim's M365 data in natural language (emails, files, Teams conversations) in a matter of seconds, where doing it manually would take hours. MFA (multi-factor authentication) blocks 99.9 per cent of account compromise attempts according to Microsoft. Without MFA, a single stolen or guessed password grants full access to Copilot and to every piece of data the user is able to view, turning Copilot into a mass exfiltration tool for the attacker.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Protection > Conditional Access > Policies
3. New policy > Name: 'CA-MFA-Copilot-Users'
4. Users: select the GRP-Copilot-Users group
5. Cloud apps: All cloud apps
6. Grant > Require multifactor authentication
7. Enable policy > Create
items.Expected: Conditional access policy enabled, targeting the Copilot group with mandatory MFA
items.Verification: Get-MgIdentityConditionalAccessPolicy | Where {$_.State -eq 'enabled'} | Select DisplayName

items.Requirement: Check that no conditional access policy blocks Microsoft Graph
items.Rationale: Microsoft Graph is the central interface through which Copilot accesses all M365 data: Exchange emails, SharePoint and OneDrive files, Teams conversations and calendar events. A conditional access policy that blocks access to Microsoft Graph cuts Copilot off from all of its data sources at once. The user will still see the Copilot button, but every request will fail with an access error. Unless this is checked beforehand with the What If tool, this kind of block often goes unnoticed because the Office applications carry on working normally.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Protection > Conditional Access > What If
3. User: select a Copilot user
4. Cloud app: Microsoft Graph
5. Click 'What If'
6. Check that the result = 'Allowed' (not 'Blocked')
7. If blocked: identify the policy and add an exclusion for the Copilot group
items.Expected: What If result = Allowed for Copilot users + Graph app
items.Verification: Get-MgIdentityConditionalAccessPolicy | Where {$_.State -eq 'enabled'} | Select DisplayName, Conditions

items.Requirement: Check that no conditional access policy blocks Office 365
items.Rationale: Copilot accesses the user's data through the Office 365 services, in particular Exchange Online for emails and SharePoint Online for files. A conditional access policy that blocks either of these services prevents Copilot from reaching the corresponding data: blocking Exchange leaves Copilot mute in Outlook, while blocking SharePoint deprives it of every file. Such blocks are common in organisations that have put device-based or location-based restrictions in place. Without a systematic check using What If, Copilot users receive baffling errors or incomplete answers.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Protection > Conditional Access > What If
3. User: a Copilot user
4. Cloud app: Office 365 (also test Office 365 Exchange Online and Office 365 SharePoint Online separately)
5. Click 'What If'
6. Check that the result = 'Allowed'
items.Expected: What If result = Allowed for Office 365, Exchange and SharePoint
items.Verification: Get-MgIdentityConditionalAccessPolicy | Where {$_.State -eq 'enabled'}

items.Requirement: User UPN = primary email address (not .local)
items.Rationale: The UPN (User Principal Name) is the identifier Copilot uses to authenticate the user and access their data through Microsoft Graph. Non-routable suffixes such as .local or .internal are not recognised by the Azure cloud services and cause silent authentication failures. The user can still sign in to Windows, but Copilot fails to retrieve their emails, files or conversations. Unless the UPNs are corrected in the on-premises Active Directory, these users will never be able to use Copilot reliably.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Users > All users
3. Sort by 'User principal name'
4. Look for UPNs ending in .local or .internal
5. If any are found: correct them in the on-premises AD > UPN Suffix property
6. Force an Entra Connect synchronisation
items.Expected: No UPN ending in .local or .internal
items.Verification: Get-MgUser -All | Where {$_.UserPrincipalName -match '\.local|\.internal'} | Select DisplayName, UserPrincipalName

items.Requirement: Remove Copilot licences from disabled accounts
items.Rationale: Every Copilot licence assigned to a disabled account is a direct waste of USD 30 per month with no benefit whatsoever to the organisation. These needlessly consumed licences reduce the number of licences available to active staff who could genuinely make use of them. On top of that, a disabled but licensed account is a security risk: if it is re-enabled by mistake or compromised, the attacker immediately has Copilot at their disposal to explore the data. Without regular clean-up, the costs accumulate and can amount to thousands of dollars a year.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Users > All users
3. Filter: Account status = Disabled
4. For each disabled account: click > Licences
5. If Microsoft 365 Copilot is ticked: untick it and save
--- OR via PowerShell ---
Get-MgUser -Filter 'accountEnabled eq false' -All | ForEach-Object { Remove-MgUserLicense -UserId $_.Id -RemoveLicenses @('<CopilotSkuId>') }
items.Expected: 0 disabled accounts holding a Copilot licence
items.Verification: Get-MgUser -Filter 'accountEnabled eq false' -All

items.Requirement: Remove Copilot licences from guest (B2B) accounts
items.Rationale: Microsoft does not officially support Copilot for guest (B2B) accounts. A licence assigned to a guest is consumed and billed, yet the behaviour is unpredictable: some features may not appear at all, and data access through Graph is limited by the very nature of a guest account. Furthermore, a guest with Copilot could potentially query data shared with them more broadly than intended. If these licences are not removed, the organisation wastes budget and exposes itself to undocumented behaviour.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Users > All users
3. Filter: User type = Guest
4. For each guest: check the assigned licences
5. If Copilot is assigned: remove the licence
items.Expected: 0 guests holding a Copilot licence
items.Verification: Get-MgUser -Filter "userType eq 'Guest'" -All

items.Requirement: Configure global SharePoint sharing and the scope of default sharing links
items.Rationale: Copilot honours existing SharePoint permissions and returns in its answers everything the user is allowed to read. If global sharing is set to 'Anyone' (anonymous links), sensitive documents can be reachable by unauthorised people and therefore surface in any employee's Copilot answers. Beyond that global setting, it is the scope of the link offered by default that drives the volume of oversharing: the current SharePoint model separates it for team sites (CoreDefaultShareLinkScope, CoreDefaultShareLinkRole) and for OneDrive (OneDriveDefaultShareLinkScope, OneDriveDefaultShareLinkRole). The distinction matters for Copilot: OneDrive is where users mix drafts, attachments and personal documents, and a default link set to 'People in your organisation' produces far more internal oversharing there than on team sites. The target value is therefore 'Specific people' with the 'View' permission, the legacy DefaultSharingLinkType and DefaultLinkPermission properties now serving only as a fallback when the module does not expose the modern parameters. Without these settings, Copilot becomes an oversharing amplifier by making poorly shared documents easy for everyone to discover.
items.Expected: SharingCapability = ExistingExternalUserSharingOnly; CoreDefaultShareLinkScope = SpecificPeople and CoreDefaultShareLinkRole = View; OneDriveDefaultShareLinkScope = SpecificPeople and OneDriveDefaultShareLinkRole = View. Organization is tolerated on team sites where the organisation documents the choice; Anyone never is.
items.Verification: Get-SPOTenant | Select-Object SharingCapability, CoreDefaultShareLinkScope, CoreDefaultShareLinkRole, OneDriveDefaultShareLinkScope, OneDriveDefaultShareLinkRole, DefaultSharingLinkType, DefaultLinkPermission
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Admin centres > SharePoint
   (or go straight to https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com)
3. Left-hand menu: Policies > Sharing
4. SharePoint slider: set it to 'New and existing guests' (second position)
5. Section 'More external sharing settings' > 'File and folder links'
6. Default link type: select 'Specific people'
7. Default permissions: select 'View'
8. Click 'Save'
--- Separate scope for OneDrive: PowerShell only ---
9. Connect-SPOService -Url https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com
10. Set-SPOTenant -CoreDefaultShareLinkScope SpecificPeople -CoreDefaultShareLinkRole View
11. Set-SPOTenant -OneDriveDefaultShareLinkScope SpecificPeople -OneDriveDefaultShareLinkRole View
12. Check the result:
    Get-SPOTenant | Select-Object SharingCapability, CoreDefaultShareLinkScope, CoreDefaultShareLinkRole, OneDriveDefaultShareLinkScope, OneDriveDefaultShareLinkRole

items.Requirement: Set anonymous sharing link expiry to a maximum of 7 days
items.Rationale: An anonymous sharing link (an 'Anyone' link) with no expiry date stays active indefinitely, even long after the original need for sharing has disappeared. Such links accumulate over time and progressively widen the surface of data reachable without authentication. Copilot can reference and cite the content of those documents in its answers to any internal user. Setting an expiry of no more than 7 days forces a conscious renewal of the share and limits exposure over time. Without this limit, sensitive documents shared on a temporary basis remain accessible forever.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Admin centres > SharePoint
   (or https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com)
2. Policies > Sharing
3. 'Anyone links' section (if anonymous sharing is allowed)
4. Tick 'These links must expire within this many days'
5. Enter '7'
6. Save
items.Expected: RequireAnonymousLinksExpireInDays <= 7
items.Verification: Get-SPOTenant | Select RequireAnonymousLinksExpireInDays

items.Requirement: Identify and restrict actual oversharing of SharePoint sites
items.Rationale: The original logic of this check measured the EXTERNAL sharing capability configured on each site (SharingCapability = ExternalUserAndGuestSharing), which is not oversharing. Yet the number one leakage vector in a Copilot context is internal: the 'Everyone except external users' (EEEU) claim applied to a site or to an item, which makes the content discoverable by the whole organisation. An HR site closed to external sharing but carrying EEEU on its payroll library used to pass this check while being the most severe exposure in the tenant: before Copilot those documents were technically reachable but hard to find; with Copilot, one natural language question is enough. Detecting sensitivity from keywords in the site title is, moreover, only a fragile heuristic. The check now relies on the data access governance reports EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite and EveryoneExceptExternalUsersForItems, complemented by the PermissionedUsers baseline that gives the number of users actually permissioned on each site; external sharing capability remains only a secondary signal. Every occurrence must be remediated, or covered by Restricted Content Discovery or Restricted Access Control until it is.
items.Expected: No business-sensitive site (HR, Finance, Executive, Legal) in the EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite or EveryoneExceptExternalUsersForItems reports. The PermissionedUsers report lists no sensitive site whose number of permissioned users exceeds the threshold set by the organisation (default: 10% of tenant headcount). Every occurrence is either remediated or covered by Restricted Content Discovery or Restricted Access Control until it is.
items.Verification: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite -Workload SharePoint ; Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsersForItems -Workload SharePoint ; Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers -Workload SharePoint
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Admin centres > SharePoint
   (or https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com)
2. Left menu: Reports > Data access governance
3. Open the 'Everyone except external users' report at site level,
   then at item level
4. Address HR, Finance, Executive and Legal sites first
--- Or with PowerShell (read-only) ---
5. Connect-SPOService -Url https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com
6. Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite -Workload SharePoint
7. Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers -Workload SharePoint
8. Download the per-site detail:
   Export-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportID <guid> -DownloadPath <path>
--- Remediation ---
9. Remove the EEEU claim from sensitive sites and libraries
10. Otherwise, cover the site until it is fixed:
    Set-SPOSite -Identity <url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true
--- Note ---
The reports require SharePoint Advanced Management, included with Microsoft 365 Copilot.
The SharePoint Advanced Management Administrator role is required for item-level
detail (module 16.0.27215.12000 or later).
items.RequiresLicense: SharePoint Advanced Management (included with Microsoft 365 Copilot)

items.Requirement: Provision OneDrive for all Copilot users
items.Rationale: OneDrive is each user's personal storage space and an important data source for Copilot: draft documents, personal notes, files received as attachments and local backups. If a user's OneDrive site is not provisioned, Copilot cannot reach their personal files and its answers are less relevant, limited to shared SharePoint files and emails. Pre-provisioning in bulk avoids the creation delay at first sign-in (which can take several hours) and guarantees that Copilot is fully operational from day one.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Admin centres > SharePoint
   (or https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com)
2. Left-hand menu: Settings
3. OneDrive section: check the storage and provisioning settings
--- Bulk provisioning (recommended method) ---
1. Open PowerShell
2. Connect-SPOService -Url https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com
3. $users = Get-MgUser -All | Select -Expand UserPrincipalName
4. Request-SPOPersonalSite -UserEmails $users -NoWait
5. Allow 24h for full propagation
--- Note ---
Provisioning also happens automatically the first time the user signs in to OneDrive or Office.com
items.Expected: Every Copilot user has an active OneDrive site
items.Verification: Get-SPOSite -IncludePersonalSite $true -Limit All -Filter "Url -like '-my.sharepoint.com'"

items.Requirement: Check that the semantic index returns content (Retrieval probe)
items.Rationale: This requirement is Blocking yet was classified as Manual: it asked the auditor to type a query into the microsoft365.com search box and judge the result by eye. It was the most important requirement in the reference list left without evidence. The Microsoft 365 Copilot Retrieval API, available in v1.0, performs exactly that test: it returns text extracts from SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot connectors that the calling user is allowed to read, through the same retrieval path as Copilot. An empty response to a query about known, indexed content proves the grounding chain is broken, something no other requirement detects: NoCrawl enabled, Restricted SharePoint Search scoped too narrowly, Restricted Content Discovery, or simply a semantic index that has not propagated yet. Microsoft documents that the index takes from a few hours to two or three days to synchronise after licences are enabled, and that new SharePoint documents accessible to at least two users are indexed daily: this check must therefore be replayed after the propagation delay, not on the day licences are assigned. The call is a POST but remains strictly a read: it changes nothing in the tenant. Without a reference term supplied to the engine, the check stays manual rather than producing a false finding.
items.Expected: The POST /copilot/retrieval call returns 200 with a non-empty retrievalHits array for a query about known, indexed reference content, and the webUrl values returned match the expected sites. An empty retrievalHits array for reference content is a blocking failure. Replay this check at least 72 hours after the first licences were assigned.
items.Verification: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/retrieval with body { "queryString": "<reference phrase>", "dataSource": "sharePoint", "maximumNumberOfResults": 10 } ; engine: -RetrievalProbeTerm '<reference phrase>'
items.HowTo:
--- Probe automated by the engine ---
1. Choose a phrase about a known, indexed reference document
   (internal procedure, HR policy, memo published more than 72 hours ago)
2. Run the engine again with -RetrievalProbeTerm '<reference phrase>'
3. The probe account must hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and the delegated
   Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All permissions
   (ExternalItem.Read.All to query Copilot connectors)
--- Equivalent manual check ---
4. Open https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer
5. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/retrieval
   { "queryString": "<reference phrase>", "dataSource": "sharePoint",
     "resourceMetadata": ["title","author"], "maximumNumberOfResults": 10 }
6. Check that retrievalHits is not empty and that the webUrl values match
   the expected sites
--- If the result is empty ---
7. Check index propagation since licence assignment
8. Check NoCrawl on the reference site (Get-PnPWeb -Includes NoCrawl)
9. Check Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchMode and the allowed list
10. Check Restricted Content Discovery on the site
    (Get-SPOSite -Identity <url> | Select-Object RestrictContentOrgWideSearch)
--- Note ---
Application permissions are not supported: a delegated token is mandatory.
The filterExpression parameter accepts KQL, for example
path:"https://tenant.sharepoint.com/sites/HR/" to target one specific site.

items.Requirement: Control exclusion from Copilot discovery (Restricted Content Discovery)
items.Rationale: An honest conclusion on NoCrawl: the Web.NoCrawl property is still not exposed by Microsoft Graph, it is only reachable through SharePoint CSOM/REST, hence through PnP.PowerShell (Get-PnPWeb -Includes NoCrawl), a community module unsupported by Microsoft, and only one site at a time. Querying several thousand sites that way is not viable inside an audit engine. The mechanism that actually excludes a site from Copilot today is no longer NoCrawl but Restricted Content Discovery (RCD), fully scriptable with the official Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell module: RCD removes the site from organisation-wide discovery and also removes its AI entry points (Copilot button, AI actions, agent creation). The check therefore inventories the sites under RCD and verifies that management of the restriction is not delegated to site administrators, in which case the scope actually excluded can no longer be guaranteed. A site under RCD is a legitimate posture: it raises a warning so the auditor can confirm the restriction is intended and documented, never an automatic finding. Without this check, whole sites stay invisible to Copilot with nobody knowing why.
items.Expected: Get-SPOTenant | Select DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement = False unless explicitly decided otherwise; the Restricted Content Discovery report lists only deliberately restricted and documented sites; RestrictContentOrgWideSearch = False on all business-critical sites. NoCrawl = False (secondary, per-site check through PnP.PowerShell).
items.Verification: Get-SPORestrictedContentDiscoverabilityReport ; Get-SPOSite -Identity <url> | Select-Object RestrictContentOrgWideSearch ; Get-SPOTenant | Select-Object DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement
items.HowTo:
1. Connect-SPOService -Url https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com
2. List the Restricted Content Discovery reports already generated:
   Get-SPORestrictedContentDiscoverabilityReport
3. Download the detail of one report:
   Get-SPORestrictedContentDiscoverabilityReport -Action Download -ReportId <guid>
4. Check one specific site:
   Get-SPOSite -Identity <url> | Select-Object RestrictContentOrgWideSearch
5. Check the delegation:
   Get-SPOTenant | Select-Object DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement
--- Remediation ---
6. Make a business site visible to Copilot again:
   Set-SPOSite -Identity <url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $false
7. Take back control of the restriction:
   Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $false
--- NoCrawl: secondary, per-site check ---
8. Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/sites/<site> -Interactive
9. Get-PnPWeb -Includes NoCrawl
10. If NoCrawl = True: Set-PnPWeb -NoCrawl $false
--- Note ---
Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management
and a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. PnP.PowerShell is a community module
unsupported by Microsoft and needs a dedicated Entra ID application.
items.RequiresLicense: SharePoint Advanced Management (included with Microsoft 365 Copilot)

items.Requirement: Verify the exit from Restricted SharePoint Search
items.Rationale: Restricted SharePoint Search limits the Microsoft Search index to the sites on an allowed list, capped at 100 sites. The mechanism was designed as a temporary measure, buying time to deal with oversharing: Microsoft has retired it and blocks any new enablement from 31 July 2026, calling for a move to Restricted Content Discovery, which restricts visibility site by site without degrading search across the rest of the tenant. For as long as Restricted SharePoint Search stays on, Copilot ignores every site outside the list, including those the user has access to, and search is impoverished for all users, including those with no Copilot licence. Keeping the mechanism is therefore no longer a target posture but a gap to close, with an exit plan backed by the Data Access Governance reports. The official read command is Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchMode, complemented by Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchAllowedList: the IsContentAccessGoverned property is only a fallback for older modules.
items.Expected: Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchMode = Disabled. If the mechanism is still on: a gap to close, with the allowed list documented (Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchAllowedList, 100 sites maximum) and a planned exit date.
items.Verification: Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchMode ; Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchAllowedList
items.HowTo:
--- Configuration through PowerShell only ---
1. Connect-SPOService -Url https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com
2. Read the current state:
   Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchMode
3. If the mode is Enabled, list the allowed sites:
   Get-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchAllowedList
4. Deal with oversharing on the sites concerned, using the Data Access Governance
   reports in the SharePoint admin centre
5. Exit the mechanism:
   Set-SPOTenantRestrictedSearchMode -Mode Disabled
6. Then restrict visibility site by site (Restricted Content Discovery):
   Set-SPOSite -Identity <url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true
--- Note ---
There is NO graphical interface for this setting.
The allowed list is capped at 100 sites and any new enablement has been
blocked since 31 July 2026.

items.Requirement: Set the OneDrive quota to a minimum of 1 TB
items.Rationale: The OneDrive quota determines how many personal files each user can store in the cloud. Too small a quota forces users to keep their files locally or on network shares, out of Copilot's reach. The larger the volume of files held in OneDrive, the more context Copilot has to deliver relevant, personalised answers. The standard quota of 1 TB per user is included in E3/E5 licences and is amply sufficient for most cases. Without an adequate quota, users work around OneDrive and Copilot loses an essential data source.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Admin centres > SharePoint
   (or https://<tenant>-admin.sharepoint.com)
2. Settings > OneDrive settings
3. 'Storage' section
4. Check that the default quota is >= 1048576 MB (1 TB)
5. If it is lower: change it and save
items.Expected: OneDriveStorageQuota >= 1048576 MB (1 TB)
items.Verification: Get-SPOTenant | Select OneDriveStorageQuota

items.Requirement: Check that every Copilot-licensed user has a primary mailbox in Exchange Online
items.Rationale: Microsoft supports Copilot only on the primary mailbox hosted in Exchange Online: the archive mailbox, group mailboxes, and shared or delegated mailboxes are all out of scope. A check that merely counts RecipientTypeDetails across a sample of mailboxes misses the case most frequently reported by practitioners: the Copilot-licensed user who has no mailbox at all (service account, shop-floor or factory account, account created without an Exchange plan, shared identity); nor does it see a Copilot licence mistakenly assigned to a shared mailbox or a resource mailbox. Without a primary mailbox in Exchange Online, Copilot fails silently for that user: the licence is consumed and the button may appear, but mailbox grounding and the storage of prompts and responses are impossible; email summarisation, draft generation and coaching by Copilot do not work. Mailboxes still held on an on-premises Exchange server are not reachable by Copilot, even in a hybrid configuration. The check therefore cross-references the list of users holding the Copilot SKU with the Exchange Online mailbox inventory and raises a named finding per user, rather than a single global statistic.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com
2. Recipients > Mailboxes: the type must be 'User mailbox'
3. Compare that list with the Copilot-licensed users (Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Your products)
4. Any Copilot licence assigned to a shared mailbox, a resource mailbox or an account with no mailbox must be removed or reassigned
--- PowerShell check ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline ; Connect-MgGraph -Scopes User.Read.All,Organization.Read.All
2. $mbx = Get-EXOMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -PropertySets Minimum
3. $sku = (Get-MgSubscribedSku | Where-Object SkuPartNumber -like '*COPILOT*').SkuId
4. $users = Get-MgUser -All -Filter "assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq $sku)" -Property UserPrincipalName,AccountEnabled,UserType
5. List the licensed UPNs missing from $mbx, or whose RecipientTypeDetails is not UserMailbox
items.Expected: 100% of users holding the Microsoft 365 Copilot SKU have RecipientTypeDetails = UserMailbox in Exchange Online (0 user without a mailbox, 0 RemoteUserMailbox, 0 Copilot licence on a shared or resource mailbox)
items.Verification: Get-EXOMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -PropertySets Minimum | Select UserPrincipalName, RecipientTypeDetails ; compare with the UPNs from Get-MgUser -All -Filter "assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq <CopilotSkuId>)" -Property UserPrincipalName,AccountEnabled

items.Requirement: Check that MAPI is enabled on the Copilot mailboxes
items.Rationale: MAPI (Messaging Application Programming Interface) is the communication protocol between the Outlook desktop client and Exchange Online. It is through this channel that Copilot in Outlook accesses email in order to generate summaries, write drafts and offer tone coaching. If MAPI is disabled on a user's mailbox, Outlook desktop cannot connect to Exchange and every Copilot feature in Outlook is inoperative. This deactivation is sometimes applied by mistake during security configuration work. Without MAPI, the user has to fall back on Outlook Web, which diminishes the Copilot experience.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com
2. Recipients > Mailboxes
3. Select the mailbox of a Copilot user
4. 'General' tab
5. 'Email apps and mobile devices' section
6. Click 'Manage email apps settings'
7. Check that 'Outlook desktop (MAPI)' = Enabled
8. If it is disabled: enable it and save
--- Bulk check through PowerShell ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline
2. Get-CASMailbox -ResultSize 50 | Where {$_.MAPIEnabled -eq $false}
3. If there are results: Set-CASMailbox -Identity user@domain.com -MAPIEnabled $true
items.Expected: MAPIEnabled = True for all Copilot users
items.Verification: Get-CASMailbox -ResultSize 50 | Where {$_.MAPIEnabled -eq $false} | Select DisplayName

items.Requirement: Enable the unified audit log and mailbox auditing
items.Rationale: The unified audit log is the central logging system of Microsoft 365, which records all user activity, including interactions with Copilot (prompts submitted, responses generated, documents accessed). Without auditing enabled, the organisation has no visibility into how Copilot is being used, which data is consulted through Copilot, or whether inappropriate access is taking place. In the event of a security incident or a compliance investigation, the absence of logs makes any inquiry impossible. It is a regulatory requirement in many sectors (finance, healthcare, government) and a prerequisite for using eDiscovery with Copilot data.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://purview.microsoft.com
2. On the home page: click the 'Audit' card
   (or left-hand menu: Audit)
3. If the 'Start recording user and admin activity' banner is displayed: click it to turn auditing on
4. Check that auditing is indeed enabled (status = Enabled)
--- Exchange check ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline
2. Get-OrganizationConfig | Select AuditDisabled
3. If True: Set-OrganizationConfig -AuditDisabled $false
items.Expected: UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled = True AND AuditDisabled = False
items.Verification: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Select UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled

items.Requirement: Allow the Copilot app in the Teams policies
items.Rationale: In Teams, Copilot works as an app that must be explicitly allowed by the app permission policy. If the 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' app is blocked or missing from the allow list, users do not see Copilot in Teams: no Copilot chat, no meeting summary, no assistance in conversations. This policy is often restrictive in large organisations that tightly control Teams apps. Without explicitly allowing the Copilot app, every Copilot feature in Teams is out of reach, even for correctly licensed users.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Menu: Teams apps > Permission policies
3. Click the 'Global' policy (or the one assigned to the Copilot group)
4. 'Microsoft apps' section
5. Check that the mode is 'Allow all apps' OR that 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' is in the allowed list
6. Save
items.Expected: Microsoft 365 Copilot app = Allowed
items.Verification: Get-CsTeamsAppPermissionPolicy -Identity Global

items.Requirement: Pin Copilot to the Teams app bar
items.Rationale: Pinning Copilot to the Teams app bar makes it visible and one click away for every user, with no need to hunt for it in the app catalogue. Adoption data shows that pinning increases Copilot usage by 40 to 60 per cent compared with a deployment without pinning. Without this configuration, the majority of users never discover the Copilot app in Teams and never use the cross-application chat features, which are nonetheless the most powerful use case. Placing Copilot at the top of the app bar maximises its visibility and the return on investment of the licences.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Teams apps > Setup policies
3. Click the 'Global' policy (or the Copilot group's policy)
4. 'Pinned apps' section
5. Click 'Add apps'
6. Search for 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' > Add
7. Move it to the top of the list (drag and drop)
8. Save
items.Expected: Microsoft 365 Copilot pinned to the app bar
items.Verification: Get-CsTeamsAppSetupPolicy -Identity Global | Select -Expand PinnedAppBarApps

items.Requirement: Enable meeting transcription (mandatory for Copilot summaries)
items.Rationale: Meeting transcription is the fuel that powers Copilot in Teams. Without it, Copilot has no text to analyse and cannot generate a meeting summary, extract follow-up actions, identify the decisions taken or attribute points to participants. This is the use case users cite most often and the one that delivers the greatest time saving (30 minutes on average per meeting). Disabling transcription amounts to disabling the primary use case of Copilot in Teams and depriving the organisation of Copilot's most tangible return on investment.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Meetings > Meeting policies
3. Click the 'Global' policy (or the Copilot group's policy)
4. 'Recording & transcription' section
5. 'Transcription' > On
6. Optional but recommended: 'Automatically start transcription' > On
7. Save
8. Allow 1-2 hours for propagation to the Teams clients
items.Expected: AllowTranscription = True
items.Verification: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global | Select AllowTranscription

items.Requirement: Enable cloud recording for meetings
items.Rationale: Cloud recording of Teams meetings allows Copilot to deliver more complete and more accurate post-meeting summaries by combining the text transcript with the audio and video context. Recordings are stored automatically in OneDrive or SharePoint and become available to Copilot for participants who were unable to attend the meeting. Without cloud recording, Copilot can only provide summaries to the participants who were present and loses the context of presentations shared on screen. Enabling recording maximises the value of every meeting by making it searchable and summarisable by Copilot at any time.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Meetings > Meeting policies
3. 'Global' policy (or the Copilot group)
4. 'Recording & transcription' section
5. 'Cloud recording' > On
6. Save
items.Expected: AllowCloudRecording = True
items.Verification: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global | Select AllowCloudRecording

items.Requirement: Set the Copilot mode for Teams meetings to the retained-transcript value
items.Rationale: The official Set/Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy parameter is -Copilot, and its four values are Enabled, EnabledWithTranscript (the service default), EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn and Disabled. Requiring merely 'Enabled, not Disabled' signs off a configuration that does not deliver the use case: Enabled is the weakest of the active values, it sets the organiser default to 'Only during the meeting', so no transcript is retained and no recap is produced after the meeting, which is precisely the benefit carrying most of the return on investment. A tenant set to Enabled would pass the check while depriving users of post-meeting summaries. The target is therefore EnabledWithTranscript or EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn, cross-checked with AllowTranscription = True: a mode that requires transcription while the policy forbids it leaves Copilot inoperative in meetings. Finally, Copilot active without a retained transcript is not neutral for compliance: Copilot prompts and responses may still be kept by Microsoft Purview retention policies, a consequence organisations often discover late. Non-global meeting policies assigned to the Copilot pilot group must be checked alongside the Global policy.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Meetings > Meeting policies
3. Select the 'Global' policy, then every policy assigned to the Copilot pilot group
4. 'Recording & transcription' section
5. 'Copilot' setting > select 'On with transcript' (EnabledWithTranscript) or 'On with transcript started automatically' (EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn)
6. Do NOT settle for 'On' (Enabled): that mode leaves the organiser default on 'Only during the meeting', with no retained transcript and no recap after the meeting
7. In the same section, check that 'Transcription' is turned on (AllowTranscription = True)
8. Save
--- Note ---
In PowerShell the parameter is -Copilot; older versions of the module expose the property as CopilotMode
items.Expected: Copilot = EnabledWithTranscript or EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn and AllowTranscription = True, on the policy applied to Copilot-licensed users
items.Verification: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global | Select-Object Identity, Copilot, AllowTranscription ; Get-CsGroupPolicyAssignment -PolicyType TeamsMeetingPolicy

items.Requirement: Enable live captions
items.Rationale: Live captions provide an additional layer of real-time text data that Copilot can draw on to improve the accuracy of its summaries and of its answers during meetings. They also improve accessibility for people who are hard of hearing and for participants joining the meeting from a noisy environment. Captions work alongside transcription and let every participant follow the conversation visually. Without captions, the experience is less inclusive and Copilot has a less rich data stream for its real-time analysis.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Meetings > Meeting policies
3. Select the 'Global' policy
4. Look for the 'Live captions' setting
5. Select 'Not enabled but the user can override' (recommended default)
6. Do NOT select 'Disabled'
7. Save
--- Note ---
This setting sits in the meeting policy's list of settings, not in a specific subsection
items.Expected: Live captions = Enabled
items.Verification: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global | Select AllowCartCaptions

items.Requirement: Enable Copilot globally at tenant level
items.Rationale: Enabling Copilot globally at tenant level is the master switch that authorises the service to operate across the whole organisation. Until this switch is turned on in the M365 admin centre, no user can see or use Copilot, whatever their licence or their individual configuration. It is the gateway to the entire deployment: without this activation, licences are consumed and billed but the service stays completely invisible in every Office application and in Teams. Propagation can take 24 to 48 hours after activation, which must be anticipated in the deployment schedule.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'View all' tab
4. The individual settings for each workload are listed
5. Check that the main settings are enabled
6. To enable/disable a setting: click on it to open its configuration
--- Note ---
The Copilot Settings page has no 'enable globally' button.
Copilot is active as soon as a user has the licence assigned.
The settings here control the individual features.
items.Expected: Copilot enabled for the organisation
items.Verification: Via admin.cloud.microsoft > Settings > Copilot (no public cmdlet)

items.Requirement: Enable all Copilot workloads (Word, Excel, PPT, Outlook, Teams, Web)
items.Rationale: Microsoft 365 Copilot lets each application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams) be enabled or disabled independently, along with the M365 web applications. By default all workloads are active, but an administrator may have disabled some of them during testing or as a precaution. A disabled workload makes Copilot completely invisible in the corresponding application: for example, disabling the Excel workload removes the Copilot button from Excel for all users. Many users reach M365 through a web browser; if the web workload is disabled, those users have no access to Copilot at all. Without checking each workload, some applications may appear not to support Copilot when the problem is simply an unticked box in the admin centre.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'View all' tab
4. Each workload is an individual setting in the list
5. Copilot is active by default in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams as soon as the licence is assigned
6. To check the web apps: click on the corresponding setting
--- Test ---
1. Open https://www.office.com with a Copilot-licensed user
2. Open a Word Online document
3. Check that the Copilot button appears in the ribbon
items.Expected: All workloads = Enabled (Word, Excel, PPT, Outlook, Teams) and M365 web applications
items.Verification: Via admin.cloud.microsoft > Settings > Copilot

items.Requirement: Enable and pin Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
items.Rationale: Copilot Chat is the unified conversational interface that queries every Microsoft 365 source at once: messages, SharePoint and OneDrive files, Teams conversations and calendar. It is the main differentiator of Microsoft 365 Copilot over generic AI tools, because it has the organisation's context. Two elements date the previous wording of this requirement. First, the entry point to test: copilot.microsoft.com is the consumer entry point tied to a personal Microsoft account, whereas the enterprise entry point is the Microsoft 365 Copilot app or copilot.cloud.microsoft, and testing the wrong address produces a false negative. Second, the scope of the setting: since 25 July 2025 for EEA and Swiss tenants, and since 28 January 2026 for all others, Copilot Chat can no longer be unpinned from the navigation of the Microsoft 365 Copilot app. The 'Pin Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat' setting therefore only governs pinning in Outlook and in Teams. Its state can now be read through the API, which avoids inferring it from usage: a freshly configured tenant has no activity and was flagged as a gap, while a tenant that had been unpinned kept residual activity for weeks.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'View all' tab
4. Open 'Pin Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat'
5. Observe the pinning state for Outlook and for Microsoft Teams
6. Document the decision if pinning is removed
--- Test ---
1. Sign in to the Microsoft 365 Copilot app or to https://copilot.cloud.microsoft with a licensed user
2. Check that Copilot Chat is available
3. Do not test https://copilot.microsoft.com: that is the consumer entry point
items.Expected: Copilot Chat available to licensed users: no tenant policy unpins it (microsoft.copilot.copilotchatpinning with no value, so the default pinning applies, or an explicit enabling value). Unpinning in Outlook and Teams must be a documented decision. Functional test on the Microsoft 365 Copilot app or copilot.cloud.microsoft.
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/policySettings/microsoft.copilot.copilotchatpinning (delegated CopilotPolicySettings.Read scope), confirmed by the Copilot Chat last activity date in the usage report

items.Requirement: Decide on Copilot access to web content
items.Rationale: Web search allows Copilot to enrich its answers with information from the internet in addition to internal Microsoft 365 data. Restricting Copilot to Microsoft 365 data guarantees that everything stays within the tenant boundary, which is decisive for regulated sectors; opening it to the web produces richer answers but means that elements of the query context pass through the web search service. This setting can now be read through the API under the identifier microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch, which distinguishes three states that the admin centre conflates: a decision recorded in a tenant policy, an existing tenant policy that does not carry the setting, and no policy at all. That distinction is the very object of the requirement, because Microsoft documents that without a policy web search is ON by default, for Microsoft 365 Copilot as well as for Copilot Chat, unless Office optional connected experiences are themselves disabled. A regulated organisation that believes it has a Microsoft 365 only data boundary because it configured nothing is mistaken.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'View all' tab
4. Open 'Web search for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat'
5. Choose whether or not to allow access to web content
6. If the environment is sensitive (defence, healthcare, finance): disable
7. If the environment is standard: enable, which enriches the answers
8. Save, so that the decision is carried by a tenant-level policy and can therefore be evidenced
9. Document the decision and its justification in the governance file
items.Expected: Explicit decision recorded in a tenant-level policy: microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch returns a non-null value, 0 for a regulated environment or 1 for a standard environment, documented in either case. A null value means the decision was never taken: web search is then on by default.
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/policySettings/microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch (beta, delegated CopilotPolicySettings.Read scope; no application permission exists)

items.Requirement: Verify the Copilot rollout app by app
items.Rationale: Verifying the rollout is the validation step that must come before any large-scale deployment: between activation, licence assignment and actual availability in the apps, many factors can block Copilot silently (Conditional Access policy, connected experiences, update channel). A global observation is not enough: it does not distinguish an Outlook blocker from a Teams blocker. Version v2 of the usage report, published on v1.0 under the /copilot/reports namespace, exposes a last activity date per application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, Loop, Teams, Copilot Chat work and web, Edge, agents), which turns a binary observation into a usable diagnosis and removes a beta dependency from a blocking control. Two delays frame the interpretation: Copilot can take up to 24 hours to appear in an app after the licence is assigned, and the report itself lags by up to 72 hours. A check run too early produces a false failure; a check run without a defined window proves nothing.
items.HowTo:
1. Assign the Copilot licence to the pilot users
2. Wait at least 72 hours: 24 h for app propagation, up to 72 h of reporting latency
3. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot
4. Check the last activity date per application for the pilot cohort
5. Expected: Copilot Chat plus at least two apps among Word, Outlook and Teams
6. For any app with no activity at all across the whole cohort after 7 days: treat it as a configuration blocker (licence, Conditional Access, update channel, connected experiences)
7. Confirm on a workstation: open Word, Outlook and Teams with a licensed user and check that Copilot is present
items.Expected: At least 72 hours after the licences are assigned: a non-empty last activity date on Copilot Chat and on at least two apps among Word, Outlook and Teams. Any app where the whole pilot cohort stays inactive beyond 7 days must be treated as a configuration blocker, not as an adoption gap.
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail(period='D7', version='v2') (Reports.Read.All scope; in delegated mode, a Reports Reader, AI Administrator or Global Reader role)

items.Requirement: Use the Copilot usage reports: availability, freshness and concealment
items.Rationale: The Copilot usage reports measure actual adoption: active users, prompts submitted, active usage days, intensity per application. Without them it is impossible to know whether the investment delivers a return, which departments use Copilot and which need support, or to justify renewing the subscription. Microsoft also states that audit logs must not be used as a basis for usage measurement: only these reports are authoritative. Three points must be checked together. First the source: the endpoints are published on v1.0 under /copilot/reports and accept version='v2', which adds the only metrics that distinguish a user who clicked once from a genuinely engaged user; the default window moved from 30 to 28 days. Then freshness: reportRefreshDate must stay recent, since Microsoft states that data is made available within 48 hours, otherwise the report no longer describes the deployment in progress. Finally concealment: displayConcealedNames conceals identifiers in every report, which makes any per-user reconciliation, and therefore any targeting of training, impossible.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Billing and usage, or Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot
3. Check that data is present and note the displayed refresh date
4. Left-hand menu: Settings > Org settings > Reports
5. Observe whether identifiers are concealed in reports
6. If concealment is on: document that named adoption tracking is impossible, or turn it off and document the lawful basis for the tracking
7. If the data is more than three days old: run the check again after the next refresh, then raise a Microsoft support ticket if the gap persists
items.Expected: The v1.0 calls under /copilot/reports answer with version='v2' and period='D28'; reportRefreshDate is less than three days old; the state of admin/reportSettings/displayConcealedNames is recorded and documented (on = named tracking impossible, off = lawful basis for the tracking to be documented).
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail(period='D28', version='v2'); GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountSummary(period='D28', version='v2'); GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings (Reports.Read.All and ReportSettings.Read.All scopes)

items.Requirement: Verify access to the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard and its measurement prerequisites
items.Rationale: The Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard provides the impact measurement recommended by Microsoft: adoption per team, evolution over time, before and after comparison. The previous wording of this requirement pointed to insights.viva.office.com and to a 'Copilot Dashboard' access control that no longer exists: Microsoft removed that dedicated control from the admin centre along with the former PowerShell cmdlet, and access to the dashboard now follows that of the Viva Insights web app. Disabling that app also removes Copilot Analytics reporting. Three prerequisites determine whether usable data is produced, and none of them is visible from the interface: no tenant policy must disable the Viva Insights web app, the minimum group size sets the granularity of team-level analysis (10 by default, 5 minimum), and the organisational attributes Microsoft_PersonEmail, Microsoft_ManagerEmail and Microsoft_Organization must have been uploaded, without which no view by department or by manager appears. Without these, the dashboard is displayed but stays empty of any segmentation, which gives the illusion of a measurement being in place. Viva Feature Access Management policies can be read from Exchange Online, which makes the first prerequisite verifiable remotely.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Settings > Microsoft Viva > Viva Insights
2. Check that no policy disables the Viva Insights web app for the whole tenant
3. Note and document the minimum group size (10 by default, 5 minimum)
4. Check that the organisational attributes Microsoft_PersonEmail, Microsoft_ManagerEmail and Microsoft_Organization have been uploaded
5. Document the exclusion list if one exists
6. Open the Copilot Dashboard and confirm that data and segmentation are present
--- Command-line check ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline (module 3.2.0 minimum)
2. Get-VivaModuleFeature -ModuleId VivaInsights
3. Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <FeatureId>
items.Expected: No Viva Feature Access Management policy disables the Viva Insights web app or the dashboard features for the whole tenant (read through the API). Minimum group size known and documented (10 by default, 5 minimum), organisational attributes Microsoft_PersonEmail, Microsoft_ManagerEmail and Microsoft_Organization uploaded, exclusion list documented where one exists (checked in the portal).
items.Verification: Connect-ExchangeOnline (module 3.2.0 minimum); Get-VivaModuleFeature -ModuleId VivaInsights; Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <FeatureId>; expected: no policy with IsFeatureEnabled=false applying to the whole tenant

items.Requirement: Decide on Copilot image generation (Designer)
items.Rationale: Copilot can generate images through Microsoft Designer, in Copilot Chat as well as in PowerPoint. In some environments that capability is not wanted: copyright, inappropriate content, sector-specific constraints. Without explicit configuration the feature is on by default. This setting can now be read through the API under the identifier microsoft.copilot.imagegeneration, which distinguishes three states that the admin centre conflates: explicitly enabled, explicitly disabled, or never configured. For an organisation under copyright constraints, the difference between 'decided on' and 'never decided' is precisely what the audit must document, and that is what the previous manual check could not establish.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'View all' tab
4. Open 'Copilot image generation' (Copilot actions section)
5. Choose whether to enable or disable it for the organisation
6. Save, so that the decision is carried by a tenant-level policy and can therefore be evidenced
7. Document the decision in the governance file
items.Expected: Explicit decision recorded in a tenant-level policy: microsoft.copilot.imagegeneration returns a non-null value, enabled or disabled, documented in either case. A null value means the decision was never taken: image generation is then on by default.
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/policySettings/microsoft.copilot.imagegeneration (beta, delegated CopilotPolicySettings.Read scope; no application permission exists)

items.Requirement: Check the Microsoft Edge configuration policy covering Copilot
items.Rationale: The 'Copilot in Bing, Microsoft Edge and Windows' scenario on the Copilot page of the admin centre is not configurable: it is an informational page. Copilot Chat benefits from enterprise data protection as soon as the user signs in with a Microsoft Entra ID account, and Copilot in Windows has been retired for commercial accounts. The only real lever on the browser is the Microsoft Edge configuration policy, reached from Settings > Microsoft Edge > Configuration policies and deployable through Intune: it carries the browser Copilot settings, for example Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled. Asking for a toggle that does not exist produced a false verdict.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Settings > Microsoft Edge > Configuration policies (or https://intune.microsoft.com > Devices > Manage devices > Configuration)
3. Open or create the policy covering Microsoft Edge
4. Check the browser Copilot settings, for example Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled
5. Check that the policy is assigned to the target group
6. If the organisation chooses not to restrict, document that decision
items.Expected: Microsoft Edge configuration policy covering the browser Copilot settings and assigned to the target group, or a documented decision not to restrict. The 'Copilot in Bing, Edge and Windows' scenario in the admin centre is not to be configured: it is informational.
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies?$expand=settings (DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All scope), then look for Edge settingDefinitionId values containing 'copilot' and for their assignments

items.Requirement: Decide on Vision (screen and camera sharing) and publish the AI usage policy
items.Rationale: No 'AI disclaimer' setting exists in the Microsoft 365 admin centre: the original requirement matched no product setting and stayed permanently pending validation, which erodes trust in the report. The scenarios actually available under 'Copilot actions' are image generation, Vision (screen and camera sharing) and Copilot in Teams meetings. Vision, which is on by default, lets Copilot analyse the shared screen and the camera feed: its state deserves an explicit decision. The 'AI-generated content, human verification required' reminder remains an AI governance good practice, carried by the AI usage policy rather than by a portal setting.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'Copilot actions' section: open 'Screen and camera sharing' (Vision)
4. Note the state, which is on by default, and decide in line with the organisation's policy
5. Document the decision in the governance file
6. Check that the AI usage policy published to users carries the 'AI-generated content, human verification required' reminder
7. Do not look for an 'AI disclaimer' setting: it does not exist
items.Expected: Explicit, documented decision on Vision (screen and camera sharing, on by default) and an AI usage policy published to users. No 'AI disclaimer' setting is to be looked for in the portal.
items.Verification: No API: admin.cloud.microsoft > Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions > Screen and camera sharing, plus the published AI usage policy

items.Requirement: Restrict Copilot agent creation to administrators
items.Rationale: By default, every Copilot-licensed user can create agents that access the organisation's M365 data. A badly configured agent can expose sensitive data to unauthorised users by creating a shortcut to restricted data sources. As with Teams team creation (often restricted to administrators), agent creation must be limited to a controlled group of trained users. Without this restriction, any employee can create an agent that reaches HR, financial or strategic data and share it with colleagues who would not normally have access to that information.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Agents
3. Click 'Settings' at the top of the page
4. 'Allowed agent types' section: configure which agent types are allowed
5. 'User access' section: select 'Specific users/groups' instead of 'All users'
6. Add the GRP-Copilot-Admins group
7. Save
--- Note ---
The Agent Settings page has 4 sections: Allowed agent types, Sharing, Templates, User access
items.Expected: Agent creation = GRP-Copilot-Admins group only (not 'All')
items.Verification: No read API exposes the Copilot > Agents > Settings > User access setting: the finding remains a visual check in admin.cloud.microsoft. Measured counterpart provided by the engine: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages (CopilotPackages.Read.All scope, Microsoft Agent 365 licence) returns the number of agents created inside the organisation and the number of blocked agents.

items.Requirement: Control the publication scope of every agent (availableTo, deployedTo, isBlocked)
items.Rationale: The original requirement asked who may publish agents, without ever verifying the outcome. Two sources now make the actual scope of every agent observable. The Microsoft Graph Copilot package management API returns availableTo and deployedTo, whose values range from 'none' to 'all' by way of a restricted audience, together with the isBlocked flag. The Copilot Studio inventory returns properties.sharedWithViewers, whose entireTenant boolean can be true even where the administrator has NOT approved sharing with the organisation. An agent shared with the whole tenant queries Microsoft 365 data on behalf of every user who invokes it and can steer hundreds of colleagues with answers that were never validated. Detecting those agents automatically, by name, is the only way to make a controlled publication policy operative: without that reading, the policy remains an intention and nobody knows which agents are genuinely exposed to the entire organisation.
items.HowTo:
1. The engine queries the agent registry: GET /v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages
2. It retains agents whose availableTo or deployedTo is 'all', excluding Microsoft-published agents and blocked agents
3. Reconcile the resulting list against the governance approval register
4. For an unapproved agent: admin.cloud.microsoft > Copilot > Agents > select the agent > restrict the audience to a named group, or block the agent
5. Record the decision (approval or withdrawal) in the governance minutes
--- Note ---
Copilot Studio agents additionally expose properties.sharedWithViewers.entireTenant through the Power Platform inventory API, which requires a separate connection that the engine does not establish
items.Expected: No organisation-authored agent with availableTo = 'all' or deployedTo = 'all' without a recorded approval; agents shared with the whole organisation are identified by name and validated by governance
items.Verification: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages?$filter=supportedHosts/any(h:h eq 'Copilot') (CopilotPackages.Read.All scope, AI Administrator or Global Administrator role, Microsoft Agent 365 licence), then filter on availableTo eq 'all' or deployedTo eq 'all' with isBlocked eq false

items.Requirement: Control the authorised third-party extensions and plug-ins
items.Rationale: Third-party extensions and plug-ins extend Copilot's capabilities by letting it interact with external systems (CRM, ERP, project management tools), but each extension obtains access to the user's data within the scope of its permissions. A malicious or badly designed extension can exfiltrate data or alter content on the user's behalf. The principle of least privilege applies: only the extensions explicitly approved by the IT team should be allowed. Without control over extensions, the organisation opens up an additional attack surface where unvetted applications reach sensitive data through Copilot.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Settings > Integrated apps
3. 'Available apps' tab
4. Review each installed application
5. For each app: click to check the permissions requested
6. Block the applications that are not approved ('Block' button)
7. Document the list of authorised applications
--- Complete via Teams admin centre ---
1. Open https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
2. Teams apps > Manage apps
3. Filter by status 'Allowed' and check the permissions
items.Expected: Only explicitly approved extensions are active
items.Verification: Via admin.cloud.microsoft > Integrated apps

items.Requirement: Control the Microsoft Graph connectors and the permission mode of the content they index
items.Rationale: Microsoft Graph connectors pour the content of external sources (CRM, ITSM, third-party HR or document management systems) into the Microsoft Search index, where Copilot cites it exactly as it would a SharePoint file. When it is created, every connection is given a permission mode that decides everything: either the connector projects the source system permissions into the index, or it indexes the content as 'Visible to everyone'. In the latter case the entire source becomes readable and citable by Copilot for every user in the tenant, including those who hold no rights at all in the originating application: this is a documented, proven data leak, not a theoretical risk. What makes it worse is that the mode cannot be changed afterwards: fixing a badly configured connection means deleting it, re-creating it and re-indexing the whole source, which makes the decision effectively irreversible once the connection is live. The original requirement merely inventoried the active connectors and asked for security team validation, with no testable criterion: it would silently accept a connection publishing an entire CRM to the whole organisation. The engine now inventories every connection, its state and the applications allowed to manage it, then measures the observable indicator of the permission mode: a connection that honours its source permissions declares external groups, whereas a connection indexed for everyone declares none. That indicator is not proof, since the mode itself is exposed by no documented property of the API, and the decisive verdict remains the Permissions pane of the admin center; it does however turn a purely declarative control into a named list of connections to verify first.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Connectors (or Settings > Search & intelligence > Data connectors)
