items.Requirement: Office Feature Updates scheduled task active and connected experiences CDN reachable
items.Rationale: The official Copilot prerequisites page has a dedicated section: the Office Feature Updates task is required for the core Copilot experiences to work correctly in Word, PowerPoint, Excel and OneNote. That task, carried by the SDXHelper.exe process, downloads the .appx packages of the connected experiences every four hours, that is to say the very code of Copilot inside the Office applications, independently of suite updates and of the update channel chosen. Many organisations disable it in Task Scheduler for perceived performance reasons, or block its CDN at the proxy without knowing what it serves. Concrete consequence when the requirement is not met: Copilot stays frozen on an obsolete build, shows intermittent functional defects and receives none of the published fixes, while the Office version shown under File > Account is perfectly up to date. The diagnosis is close to unreachable, because neither the licence, nor the update channel, nor the tenant policies appear to be at fault, and the gap between two identical workstations stays unexplained. The measurement covers a reference workstation and proves nothing about the fleet: it must be relayed by an inventory check or a configuration policy once the issue is confirmed. The network part of the check is partial too, since the endpoints service mostly publishes wildcard URLs that cannot be resolved as such.
items.HowTo:
1. On a reference workstation, open Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc)
2. Expand Task Scheduler Library > Microsoft > Office
3. Check that the 'Office Feature Updates' and 'Office Feature Updates Logon' tasks are present and in the Ready state (never Disabled)
4. If a task is disabled, identify the group policy, the image build script or the hardening tool that disables it, and fix it at the source
5. Open https://endpoints.office.com/endpoints/worldwide?clientrequestid=<GUID> and note the URLs of entries id=46 and id=47 (connected experiences CDN)
6. Confirm with the network team that those URLs are allowed on 443, wildcards included
7. Run the engine again with -IncludeLocalChecks from that workstation to automate steps 2 to 6
items.Expected: The \Microsoft\Office\Office Feature Updates and \Microsoft\Office\Office Feature Updates Logon scheduled tasks exist and are in the Ready state (never Disabled), and the Microsoft 365 endpoints id=46 and id=47 (connected experiences CDN) are reachable on 443 from the workstation.
items.Verification: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath '\Microsoft\Office\' | Where-Object { $_.TaskName -like 'Office Feature Updates*' } | Select-Object TaskName, State; $e = Invoke-RestMethod ('https://endpoints.office.com/endpoints/worldwide?clientrequestid=' + [guid]::NewGuid()) -TimeoutSec 8; $e | Where-Object { $_.id -in 46, 47 } | Select-Object id, urls, tcpPorts

items.Requirement: WebView2 runtime present and third-party cookies allowed for the Office web applications
items.Rationale: The official Copilot prerequisites page is categorical: for Copilot to work in Word Online, Excel Online and PowerPoint Online, third-party cookies must be allowed. Blocking third-party cookies prevents Copilot licence validation in the web applications and makes the button disappear outright. Yet many organisations publish, through group policy or Intune, an Edge or Chrome configuration blocking third-party cookies for privacy reasons, without knowing it breaks Copilot. The Copilot pane of the desktop Office applications renders for its part inside the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime: its absence on a hardened workstation, a minimal VDI image or a thin client prevents the pane from opening, with no explicit error message. Concrete consequence when the requirement is not met: a whole population, the one working exclusively in the browser or on shared workstations, has no access to Copilot at all while the licence, the update channel, the tenant policies and conditional access are all compliant, and the seats concerned are billed without being usable. The diagnosis is all the slower because the symptom is reported as 'the button does not appear', a wording that systematically points investigation towards licensing. This check measures one reference workstation: a policy published on a different organisational unit may produce the opposite result elsewhere in the fleet.
items.HowTo:
1. On a reference workstation, open Microsoft Edge and browse to edge://policy to list the policies applied
2. Check that the BlockThirdPartyCookies policy is absent or set to 0, and that DefaultCookiesSetting is not 2 (block all)
3. Check that the CookiesBlockedForUrls list covers no Microsoft 365 domain, wildcards included
4. If Google Chrome is deployed, repeat steps 1 to 3 with chrome://policy
5. In the Microsoft Intune admin center: Devices > Manage devices > Configuration, open the Microsoft Edge profiles and fix the 'Block third party cookies' setting at the source
6. Check that the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is present: Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps, entry 'Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime'
7. Deploy the WebView2 runtime (Evergreen Standalone Installer) on the workstations that lack it
8. Run the engine again with -IncludeLocalChecks from that workstation to automate steps 2, 3, 4 and 6
items.Expected: On the reference workstations: the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is installed (pv value populated under EdgeUpdate\Clients); the Edge BlockThirdPartyCookies policy is absent or set to 0, likewise for Chrome; DefaultCookiesSetting is not 2; no CookiesBlockedForUrls entry covers the Microsoft 365 domains. Supported browser: Edge (recommended), Chrome, Firefox or Safari, kept up to date.
items.Verification: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\Clients\{F3017226-FE2A-4295-8BDF-00C3A9A7E4C5}' -Name pv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object pv; foreach ($p in 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome') { Get-ItemProperty -Path $p -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object PSPath, BlockThirdPartyCookies, DefaultCookiesSetting }

items.Requirement: No device-based licensing activation on the Copilot workstations
items.Rationale: The Copilot prerequisites page and the Microsoft troubleshooting article state it explicitly: Copilot is not available when Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise is activated by device licence; a user licence is mandatory. Device-based activation is common in shared-workstation environments (workshops, hospitals, call centres, kiosks, training rooms, language labs), where it is driven by the DeviceBasedLicensing property of the Office Deployment Tool or by the 'Use a device-based license for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise' group policy. Concrete consequence when the requirement is not met: the users of those workstations consume a billed Copilot licence but will never see the Copilot button, whatever the tenant configuration. The diagnosis is impossible from the admin center, since the licence, the service plan, the update channel and the policies are all compliant there: only the workstation ClickToRun registry, or the 'Belongs to: this device' wording under Word > File > Account, reveals the cause. This is one of the rare cases where a green tenant check and a red workstation check legitimately contradict each other, and where only reading the workstation settles it. The check therefore cross-references the reference workstation registry value with the possible presence of a device-based Microsoft 365 Apps subscription on the tenant, that second signal serving to scope the population to examine. Holding such a subscription is not a deviation in itself: the deviation is the combination with Copilot-licensed users working on those devices.
items.HowTo:
1. On a reference workstation, open Word then File > Account
2. Under 'Product Information', check that the wording 'Belongs to: this device' does not appear; it signals device-based activation, which is incompatible with Copilot
3. Check the O365ProPlusRetail.DeviceBasedLicensing registry value under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Office\ClickToRun\Configuration: it must be absent or different from 1
4. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft then Billing > Your products, and look for a 'Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise (device)' or 'Microsoft 365 Apps for Education (device)' subscription
5. If such a subscription exists, list the devices it covers and check that no Copilot-licensed user works on them
6. For every workstation concerned, remove the DeviceBasedLicensing property from the Office Deployment Tool configuration, disable the matching group policy, then reactivate Office with a user licence
7. Run the engine again with -IncludeLocalChecks from that workstation to automate steps 3 and 4
items.Expected: No target Copilot workstation is on a device licence: the O365ProPlusRetail.DeviceBasedLicensing registry value is absent or different from 1, and Word > File > Account does not display 'Belongs to: this device'. On the tenant side, if a Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise (device) or Microsoft 365 Apps for Education (device) subscription exists, no Copilot-licensed user works on the devices it covers.
items.Verification: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Office\ClickToRun\Configuration' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -Property '*DeviceBasedLicensing*'; Get-MgSubscribedSku -All | Where-Object { $_.SkuPartNumber -match 'DEVICE' -and $_.SkuPartNumber -match 'OFFICE|APPS|PROPLUS|M365EDU|O365' } | Select-Object SkuPartNumber, SkuId, ConsumedUnits

items.Requirement: Assign the AI Administrator role for Copilot administration and enforce least privilege
items.Rationale: Microsoft introduced the built-in Microsoft Entra AI Administrator role and now presents it as the recommended role for administering Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents without resorting to Global Administrator: it opens the Copilot Control System settings, the agent inventory and the adoption reports. Without it, organisations keep granting Global Administrator to business profiles — Copilot project manager, training lead, departmental champion — for simple settings, which multiplies highly privileged accounts over the most sensitive perimeter of the tenant and contradicts the least-privilege principle applied everywhere else in this framework. The consequence is direct: a single one of those accounts, once compromised, no longer grants access to Copilot but to the entire tenant, including the Conditional Access policies meant to protect Copilot and the audit settings that should reveal the incident. The role also lends itself to on-demand activation through Privileged Identity Management, which brings standing privilege back to zero between two interventions and leaves a time-stamped trace of every activation. The check reads the active and eligible holders, then flags the case where every holder of the role is also a Global Administrator: in that configuration the role is indeed assigned but it reduces no privilege at all, and the requirement is only met in appearance. Confirming that no account was granted Global Administrator for the sole purpose of administering Copilot remains a matter of intent, to be carried into the periodic access review. The framework so far carried no requirement at all about the administration roles of Copilot itself.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Roles and administrators > search for 'AI Administrator'
3. Assignments tab: read the active holders and the eligible holders
4. Assign the role to the staff responsible for Copilot, as an eligible assignment where Privileged Identity Management is held: Identity Governance > Privileged Identity Management > Microsoft Entra roles > Assignments
5. Roles and administrators > Global Administrator: check that no account is listed there solely for Copilot administration
6. Remove Global Administrator from those accounts once the AI Administrator role is assigned, then record the review and its date
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes RoleManagement.Read.Directory,Directory.Read.All
2. $role = Get-MgDirectoryRole -Filter "roleTemplateId eq 'd2562ede-74db-457e-a7b6-544e236ebb61'"
3. Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $role.Id
4. Compare the resulting list with the members of the Global Administrator role (roleTemplateId 62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10)
items.Expected: At least one active or eligible holder of the AI Administrator role (roleTemplateId d2562ede-74db-457e-a7b6-544e236ebb61), preferably activated on demand through Privileged Identity Management. The holders of that role are not, all of them, also Global Administrators, and no account was granted Global Administrator for the sole purpose of administering Copilot.
items.Verification: Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directoryRoles(roleTemplateId='d2562ede-74db-457e-a7b6-544e236ebb61')/members" ; Privileged Identity Management complement: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleEligibilitySchedules?$filter=roleDefinitionId eq 'd2562ede-74db-457e-a7b6-544e236ebb61'

items.Requirement: Turn Customer Lockbox on and declare at least two approvers
items.Rationale: Customer Lockbox requires the explicit approval of the organisation before a Microsoft support engineer can access tenant content during an intervention. The Microsoft Purview documentation explicitly lists Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions among the customer content covered, the coverage being delivered through Exchange Online support since prompts and responses are stored in the user's mailbox. Without Customer Lockbox, a troubleshooting access to a mailbox can therefore reach the entire history of a member of staff's Copilot interactions — and so the excerpts of confidential documents cited as grounding — with no validation by the organisation and no recorded decision on the customer side. For sectors subject to a data access control obligation, to HIPAA or to a FedRAMP-style framework, turning it on is an expected piece of audit evidence, and its absence becomes a reservation in the compliance questionnaire supplied to customers. The setting is a single checkbox, at no cost once the service plan is held, and it only has effect if it is turned on before the incident: switched on afterwards, it recovers nothing. The second half of the requirement is operational: an unanswered request expires after twelve hours, so a single approver on leave turns the mechanism into a denial suffered rather than a decision owned, and blocks a legitimate support intervention at the worst possible moment. At least two distinct approvers, with deputies named in the on-call procedure, are therefore needed for the control to produce the intended effect.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://purview.microsoft.com
2. Settings > Customer Lockbox: turn on 'Require approval for all data access requests'
3. Open https://entra.microsoft.com > Roles and administrators > search for 'Customer LockBox Access Approver'
4. Assign the role to at least two distinct, reachable accounts, and name their deputies in the on-call procedure
5. Check that the approvers do receive the email notifications and document the expected handling time (a request expires after 12 hours)
6. Record the decision procedure: who approves, against which criteria, and where the decision is traced
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline
2. Get-OrganizationConfig | Select-Object CustomerLockBoxEnabled
3. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes RoleManagement.Read.Directory
4. $role = Get-MgDirectoryRole -Filter "roleTemplateId eq '9f06204d-73c1-4d4c-880a-6edb90606fd8'" ; Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $role.Id
items.Expected: CustomerLockBoxEnabled = True at Exchange Online organisation level, and at least two distinct accounts holding the Customer LockBox Access Approver directory role, with named deputies so that requests do not expire silently after 12 hours.
items.Verification: Get-OrganizationConfig | Select-Object CustomerLockBoxEnabled ; approvers: Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directoryRoles(roleTemplateId='9f06204d-73c1-4d4c-880a-6edb90606fd8')/members"
items.RequiresLicense: Microsoft 365 E5 (or the Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance add-on)

items.Requirement: Establish the effective geography of Copilot data and the Preferred Data Location of users under Multi-Geo
items.Rationale: The content of Copilot interactions — the user prompt, the generated response, the citations of the grounding sources — together with the associated semantic index is stored at rest in the geography of the tenant, under contractual commitments that vary with the country of registration, the Advanced Data Residency subscription and the Multi-Geo add-on. In a Multi-Geo tenant, the location of the interaction content is determined by the Preferred Data Location of the user querying Copilot: if that property is not set or carries an invalid code, the data silently falls back to the primary geography of the tenant. The consequence is concrete for a European or regulated organisation: prompts containing excerpts of HR files, contracts or health data may be stored outside the announced geography, while GDPR or sector compliance was presented as settled to the security committee, and nobody notices because no alert is raised. The gap then surfaces only during a customer questionnaire, a supervisory authority review or a data subject access request, that is to say when it is too late to fix it quietly. The correction is also slow: setting the Preferred Data Location triggers the migration of the user's mailbox and OneDrive, an operation measured in days that cannot be steered under pressure. The check reads the effective geography of the tenant, the presence of a Multi-Geo or Advanced Data Residency subscription, and the share of Copilot-licensed users with no Preferred Data Location. Formalising the target geography and its legal basis in the compliance file remains a documentary act that the engine can only call for.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Data location: read the effective geography of each workload
3. Billing > Your products: check for a 'Multi-Geo Capabilities in Microsoft 365' subscription and, where relevant, for Advanced Data Residency
4. Where Multi-Geo is in place: https://entra.microsoft.com > Users > <Copilot-licensed user> > Properties > Preferred data location, and check that the value is set for every licence holder
5. Set preferredDataLocation at the synchronisation source (preferredDataLocation attribute in Microsoft Entra Connect) for synchronised accounts, directly in Microsoft Entra for cloud-only accounts
6. Check the migration of the mailbox and of OneDrive after each correction
7. Record the target geography, the legal basis retained and the review date in the compliance file
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes User.Read.All,Organization.Read.All
2. Get-MgOrganization | Select-Object CountryLetterCode, PreferredDataLocation
3. Get-MgUser -All -Filter "assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq <CopilotSkuId>)" -Property UserPrincipalName,PreferredDataLocation | Where-Object { -not $_.PreferredDataLocation }
4. Multi-Geo complement: Get-SPOGeoStorageQuota for the inventory of satellite geographies
items.Expected: The effective data location of the tenant is known, recorded and documented together with its legal basis. Where Multi-Geo is in place, 100% of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users carry a valid preferredDataLocation value. Where internal policy requires Advanced Data Residency, the corresponding subscription does cover every user of the tenant.
items.Verification: Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/organization?$select=countryLetterCode,preferredDataLocation" ; then GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$select=userPrincipalName,preferredDataLocation&$top=999 filtered on Copilot licence holders

items.Requirement: Guarantee the preservation of Copilot interactions when a member of staff leaves (retention or Litigation Hold)
items.Rationale: Copilot prompts and responses are copied into a hidden folder of the user's Exchange Online mailbox. When a member of staff leaves the organisation and their Microsoft 365 account is deleted, their Copilot interactions only survive if the mailbox becomes an inactive mailbox, that is to say only if a retention policy, a Litigation Hold or an eDiscovery hold was applied to it before the deletion. Without that hold, removing the licence and deleting the account causes the permanent loss of the history: it becomes impossible to answer a court order, to investigate a suspicion of data exfiltration through Copilot by a leaver, or to produce the items requested during a review. The risk peaks precisely on the most sensitive population, that of contentious departures, where deleting the account is often the first measure taken. This check is distinct from requirement 56: that one verifies that a retention policy exists, this one verifies that it effectively covers the mailboxes of Copilot-licensed users, which is not the same thing once policies are targeted at groups. The reading combines the three mechanisms that produce coverage: the Litigation Hold on the mailbox, the holds applied to the mailbox, and the policies declared at organisation level, from which a mailbox may be explicitly excluded. An explicit exclusion is treated as an absence of coverage: that is exactly the case that simply reading an organisation-wide policy would let through.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://purview.microsoft.com
2. Data lifecycle management > Retention policies: check that a policy covers the 'Exchange mailboxes' location and that it includes the Copilot licence assignment group
3. Check the exclusion list of the policy: an excluded mailbox is not covered, even if the policy applies to the whole organisation
4. Where no policy applies: https://admin.exchange.microsoft.com > Recipients > Mailboxes > <user> > More actions > Manage litigation hold, and turn the hold on
5. Add the 'check the hold' step to the leaver procedure, BEFORE removing the licence and deleting the account
6. Review the coverage of the Copilot-licensed population periodically and record the review
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline
2. Get-OrganizationConfig | Select-Object -ExpandProperty InPlaceHolds
3. Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -RecipientTypeDetails UserMailbox | Select-Object UserPrincipalName, LitigationHoldEnabled, @{N='Holds';E={($_.InPlaceHolds -join ';')}}
4. Cross-reference with the Copilot-licensed user principal names and isolate the mailboxes with no hold of their own and excluded from the organisation-wide policies (identifiers prefixed with a minus sign)
items.Expected: 100% of the mailboxes of users holding a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence are covered by at least one hold: LitigationHoldEnabled = True, or a non-empty InPlaceHolds, or an organisation-wide retention policy from which the mailbox is not excluded. No Copilot user should appear without any of those three forms of coverage.
items.Verification: Get-Mailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -RecipientTypeDetails UserMailbox | Select-Object UserPrincipalName, LitigationHoldEnabled, InPlaceHolds ; cross-reference with Get-OrganizationConfig | Select-Object InPlaceHolds and with the list of Copilot-licensed user principal names from Microsoft Graph

items.Requirement: Rule on third-party AI subprocessors and forbid preview models with data retention
items.Rationale: Microsoft has brought third-party model providers in as subprocessors of Microsoft 365 Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio and Copilot in the Microsoft 365 apps. The 'AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors' setting is turned on by default for most commercial cloud customers, and turned off by default for tenants in the European Union, the EFTA and the United Kingdom: a multinational organisation may therefore sit in two different situations depending on the tenant, without ever having decided so. The critical point is the 'Preview models with Data Retention' sub-setting: models labelled that way fall outside the Microsoft contractual framework, the provider acts there as an independent data controller, retains most inputs and outputs for up to 30 days, some content for up to two years and classification scores for up to seven years. Turning them on without a formal decision amounts to transferring corporate data outside the Microsoft Data Protection Addendum, which is a proven data exposure and a potential GDPR breach, the subprocessor not being declared in the record of processing activities. Those models are also excluded from the EU Data Boundary and from the in-country processing commitments, which makes the decision incompatible with any sovereignty requirement left unarbitrated. No Microsoft Graph API and no public cmdlet exposes the state of this setting: the requirement stays manual, but it does bear on a real tenant setting rather than on general advice, which is why it remains scored. The expected value is therefore not a technical value but a documented, dated decision owned by the compliance lead.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Copilot > Settings > View all
3. Search for 'AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors' (AI Administrator or Global Administrator role)
4. Record the value of the setting and the scope of authorised users or groups
5. Check that the 'Preview models with Data Retention' sub-setting stays on 'No users'
6. Where an opening is requested: have the compliance lead accept the provider's commercial terms and data processing addendum in writing, restrict the scope to an explicitly approved group, and register the subprocessor in the record of processing activities
7. Schedule a review of the decision whenever the Message center announces a new subprocessor
--- Establishing the state ---
No Microsoft Graph endpoint and no public cmdlet exposes this setting: the state is established visually and the evidence is the written decision.
items.Expected: A documented and traceable decision for the 'AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors' setting: the state retained, the scope of authorised users or groups, the date and the signatory. The 'Preview models with Data Retention' sub-setting stays on 'No users', unless the compliance lead has formally accepted the provider terms and data processing addendum in writing, with registration in the record of processing activities. For a tenant subject to a European sovereignty requirement: third-party subprocessors turned off, or restricted to an explicitly approved group.
items.Verification: Manual check: https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Copilot > Settings > View all > 'AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors'. Expected evidence: a dated written decision, the authorised scope, and registration in the record of processing activities.

items.Requirement: Align the flex routing setting with sovereignty requirements and the EU Data Boundary
items.Rationale: Flex routing is a tenant setting introduced for customers within the EU Data Boundary: when it is on, large language model inference for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat may run outside that boundary — in the United States, Canada or Australia — during peak load periods, and pseudonymised data may be stored outside the boundary. The setting is turned on by default for eligible tenants created after 25 March 2026, which means a European public sector or regulated organisation may end up in breach of its own sovereignty policy without having done or signed anything. Without an explicit check, the exposure is discovered during an audit, a customer questionnaire or a referral to the data protection authority, whereas the switch itself is instant, reversible and free. The stake is not only legal: for an operator of essential services or a healthcare provider, the commitment to process within the European boundary is often an enforceable contractual clause, and breaching it is paid for in penalties or lost business. The setting is not displayed for tenants that have purchased Multi-Geo, nor for tenants outside the EU Data Boundary scope: that absence must then be established and its cause documented, otherwise an auditor cannot tell an absent setting from an unchecked one. An equivalent setting exists on the Power Platform side for Copilot Studio and Dynamics 365: a decision taken on one side only leaves the other channel open. No Microsoft Graph API and no public cmdlet exposes this state: the requirement stays manual and the expected value is a documented decision, not a technical value.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Copilot > Settings > View all
3. Search for 'Flex routing during peak load periods' (AI Administrator role)
4. Record the value of the setting. If the setting does not appear, establish and document the cause: tenant outside the EU Data Boundary scope, or Multi-Geo in place
5. For any entity subject to an EU processing requirement (public sector, healthcare, defence, operators of essential services): choose 'Do not allow flex routing'
6. Otherwise, own 'Allow flex routing' through a written decision accompanied by its risk analysis
7. Check the equivalent setting in the Power Platform admin center for Copilot Studio and Dynamics 365, then set a review date
--- Establishing the state ---
No Microsoft Graph endpoint and no public cmdlet exposes this setting: the state is established visually and the evidence is the written decision.
items.Expected: A documented decision: 'Do not allow flex routing' for any organisation subject to an EU processing requirement, or 'Allow flex routing' owned and recorded together with its risk analysis and review date. Where the setting is absent from the console, the cause is established and documented (tenant outside the EU Data Boundary scope, or Multi-Geo in place). The equivalent decision is taken on the Power Platform side.
items.Verification: Manual check: https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Copilot > Settings > View all > 'Flex routing during peak load periods' ; equivalent setting in the Power Platform admin center. Expected evidence: a dated written decision and its risk analysis.

items.Requirement: Rule on Copilot limited mode in Teams meetings (analysis of how participants felt)
items.Rationale: Limited mode prevents Copilot, in Teams meetings, from answering prompts about the feelings and emotions of the participants — of the kind 'what was the mood in the room' or 'who seemed opposed to the project'. None of requirements 27 to 32 covers this point: they stop at transcription, recording and the meeting Copilot mode. Yet in French and European organisations, analysing the sentiment of identified employees in a meeting is precisely the subject that triggers opposition from the works council and questions from the data protection officer, and it may amount to processing special categories of data. The consequence of having no position is twofold: either the subject is raised by an employee and freezes the rollout at the worst moment, or it is never raised and the organisation keeps an unarbitrated processing activity in its record. The setting is driven per group, which allows a differentiated rollout — limited mode on for the sensitive population, off for a pilot scope that has been explicitly informed — and it is now readable in Microsoft Graph v1.0, which makes it an automatable check. Reading it, however, only exists as a delegated permission: in application context the engine declares the check not evaluated, which signals a gap in the audit perimeter and not a configuration gap. The check establishes the position actually in force; formalising the employee relations decision remains documentary evidence.
items.HowTo:
1. Establish the position in force: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/settings/limitedMode (delegated CopilotSettings-LimitedMode.Read permission, Global Reader role at minimum)
2. Read isEnabledForGroup and groupId, then identify the target group in https://entra.microsoft.com > Groups
3. Compare the observed scope with the scope decided with the data protection officer and the staff representatives
4. While the employee relations decision is not formalised: turn limited mode on for the group of Copilot-licensed users
5. Apply the setting: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/settings/limitedMode with isEnabledForGroup and groupId (delegated CopilotSettings-LimitedMode.ReadWrite permission)
6. Record the decision, its scope, the date the staff representatives were consulted and the review date
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes CopilotSettings-LimitedMode.Read
2. Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/settings/limitedMode"

items.Requirement: Decide explicitly on access to the Frontier programme (Copilot preview features)
items.Rationale: Microsoft introduced an audience-based release model for Copilot: the opt-in Frontier programme, standard release and delayed release. Frontier gives access to experimental features and agents before general availability, sometimes backed by language models from third-party providers that must be approved separately in the tenant. The default value is 'No access', which is the right setting for a production tenant, but switching to 'All users' takes one click and turns the whole estate into a test cohort: features liable to change without notice, undocumented behaviours, support tickets that are not covered, and checks in this framework bearing on settings that do not yet exist in the released version. Conversely, never opening Frontier to a pilot group deprives the organisation of any ability to anticipate forthcoming changes and condemns it to absorb every evolution in production. This setting must therefore be the object of an explicit, documented and reviewed decision, on the same footing as access to web content. The setting bears on the tenant's exposure to preview features: it is genuinely controllable and scored, and must not be confused with a capability that is itself in preview and would fall out of the score. No API exposes it to date — the beta copilotPolicySetting resource only covers copilotchatpinning, blockaccesstoopenfiles, imagegeneration, allowwebsearch and allowinadmincenters — which makes the state visual and the evidence documentary.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Copilot > Settings > 'View all' tab
3. Search for 'Frontier' then open 'Copilot Frontier' (accepted roles: AI Administrator, Security Administrator, Office Apps Administrator)
4. Record the value in force among 'No access', 'Specific users' and 'All users'
5. Where the value is 'All users': bring it back to 'No access', or to 'Specific users' targeted at a named pilot group representing less than 10 per cent of the licences
6. Check that any third-party provider models required by the preview features have been explicitly approved
7. Record the decision, the pilot group, the owner of the feedback loop and the review date
--- Establishing the state ---
No API exposes this setting: the state is established visually and the evidence is the written decision.
items.Expected: Copilot Frontier = 'No access' (the default) or 'Specific users' targeted at a named pilot group representing less than 10% of the licences; never 'All users' in production. The decision, the owner of the feedback loop and the review date are documented, and any third-party provider models required have been explicitly approved.

items.Requirement: Identify and reclaim dormant Copilot licences assigned to active accounts
items.Rationale: The framework already checks that Copilot licences are not wasted on disabled accounts (requirement 14) or on guests (requirement 15), but no check detects the largest source of waste in practice: the active, valid, licensed account that has never issued a single prompt. The admin center shows licences consumed, never licences used: an organisation can therefore renew seats nobody uses for years without ever noticing. At roughly USD 30 per seat per month, a hundred dormant licences represent USD 36,000 a year of spend with nothing in return, and as many seats denied to the staff who are asking for them. The Copilot usage report exposes, per user, a last activity date per application and, in its v2 version, the number of prompts submitted and the number of active usage days: cross-referenced with the list of licence holders, it produces an objective reclaim metric. This is the figure the finance department asks for at renewal time, and the only one that allows a choice between reducing the volume purchased and investing in user enablement. Two technical conditions govern the measurement: the audit account must hold the Reports.Read.All permission or a report-reading role, and report anonymisation must be turned off, otherwise the identifiers are hashed and the licence-by-licence cross-reference becomes impossible. Without this check, the Operate phase described by Microsoft amounts to counting purchases, and the real cost of the Copilot estate is never confronted with its real usage.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Settings > Org settings > Reports: clear the option that displays concealed user names, otherwise the user principal names are hashed
3. Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot: select the 90-day period and read the last activity column
4. Billing > Your products > Microsoft 365 Copilot: compare the number of assigned seats with the number of active users in the report
5. Draw up the list of seats with no activity at all over 90 days and confirm it with the managers concerned
6. Remove each seat confirmed as dormant by taking the user out of the licence assignment group: https://entra.microsoft.com > Groups > <Copilot group> > Members
7. Reassign the freed licences to the users on the waiting list and record the decision
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes Reports.Read.All,User.Read.All,Organization.Read.All
2. $sku = (Get-MgSubscribedSku | Where-Object SkuPartNumber -like '*COPILOT*').SkuId
3. $users = Get-MgUser -All -Filter "assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq $sku)" -Property UserPrincipalName,AccountEnabled
4. $usage = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail(period='D90')"
5. Compare the active user principal names in $users with the rows of $usage whose last activity date is empty
items.Expected: 0 users holding a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence on an active account with an empty last activity date over 90 days (period='D90'). The activation rate at 28 and 90 days is recorded and compared from one audit to the next; every licence with no prompt at all over 90 days appears on a reassignment list.

items.Requirement: Settle and document the Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat perimeter for the unlicensed population
items.Rationale: The framework implicitly assumes that Copilot only exists once a Copilot licence has been assigned. That assumption has been wrong since January 2025: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is available at no extra cost to every Entra user holding a Microsoft 365 or Office E1 to E5, F1, F3, Business or A1 to A5 licence, or even Teams alone, and it is pinned by default for most of them. An organisation deploying 200 Copilot licences therefore already has, in practice, several thousand users on Copilot Chat: an entirely separate denominator from the licensed population, one that escapes every other check in the framework. Two decisions must be taken before go-live. The first concerns exposure: unlicensed Copilot Chat is grounded on the web, but as soon as usage-based billing is enabled, metered agents can be grounded on the tenant's SharePoint data for those same unlicensed users. The second concerns restriction: if the organisation wants to reserve Copilot Chat for licensed users, the only documented method goes through the Integrated apps portal by targeting a group, bearing in mind that blocking the app organisation-wide would also cut off licensed users. Without that decision, the organisation discovers after the fact that tenant data has been used by a population it believed to be out of scope, and that its acceptable-use policy covers only a fraction of its real users. Microsoft states that unlicensed Copilot Chat usage is exposed by no Graph reporting API: only the unified audit log makes it measurable.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: read the usage volumes for the unlicensed population
3. Settings > Integrated apps > Microsoft 365 Copilot: check the access option in force ('Everyone', or 'Specific users/groups')
4. If Copilot Chat is to be reserved for licensed users: choose 'Specific users/groups' and target the Copilot licence assignment group. Never block the app organisation-wide: that would also cut off licensed users
5. Copilot > Billing and usage: check the decision taken on usage-based billing for metered agents, which is off by default
6. Record the three decisions in the design note: Copilot Chat perimeter, usage-based billing, observed volumes
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-ExchangeOnline ; Connect-MgGraph -Scopes User.Read.All,Organization.Read.All
2. $audit = Search-UnifiedAuditLog -RecordType CopilotInteraction -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) -EndDate (Get-Date) -ResultSize 5000
3. $sku = (Get-MgSubscribedSku | Where-Object SkuPartNumber -like '*COPILOT*').SkuId
4. $licensed = (Get-MgUser -All -Filter "assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq $sku)" -Property UserPrincipalName).UserPrincipalName
5. $audit.UserIds | Sort-Object -Unique | Where-Object { $_ -notin $licensed }
items.Expected: A formal decision on three points: the Copilot Chat perimeter for the unlicensed population, whether usage-based billing is enabled for metered agents, and the real volume of unlicensed usage observed. 0 unlicensed users interacting with an agent grounded on tenant data without the usage-based billing decision having been taken and documented.
items.Verification: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -RecordType CopilotInteraction -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) -EndDate (Get-Date) -ResultSize 5000 ; cross-reference the UserIds obtained with Get-MgUser -All -Filter "assignedLicenses/any(x:x/skuId eq <CopilotSkuId>)" -Property UserPrincipalName

items.Requirement: Govern usage-based billing for agents: billing policy, perimeter, budget and Copilot Credits tracking
items.Rationale: The Copilot economic model is no longer limited to the monthly seat: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat agents and SharePoint agents are billed by consumption in Copilot Credits (1 credit = USD 0.01) against an Azure subscription, through a billing policy created in the admin center and then connected to the service concerned. Two symmetrical risks follow. Without a billing policy created and connected, the agents concerned simply do not work for the users targeted: the organisation believes it has deployed a capability that stays inert, and tickets come in without the cause being visible anywhere in the Copilot settings. Conversely, an active policy with no budget exposes the organisation to uncapped cost drift, because Microsoft states that the budget raises notifications but is never enforced: consumption continues beyond the amount defined. Requirements 43 to 51 govern agents, but none addresses their billing prerequisite or the management of the associated cost. The policy further requires an Azure subscription in the same tenant, a resource group and the Owner or Contributor role on that subscription, which implies coordination between the Microsoft 365 administration and the Azure team. No Microsoft Graph API and no public cmdlet exposes billing policies or credit consumption to date: this requirement is therefore informative, it appears in the report with its procedure but does not weigh on the compliance score.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Copilot > Billing and usage > 'Billing policies' tab (accepted roles: Billing Administrator, AI Administrator or Global Administrator)
3. Check that a policy exists, that it points to an Azure subscription in the same tenant and to a resource group
4. 'Usage-based services' tab: check that the policy is connected to the service concerned (Copilot Chat agents, SharePoint agents)
5. Set a budget and its notifications, and name the owner who receives them. Remember: the budget notifies but does not cap consumption
6. Reports > Usage > Copilot Credits: track monthly consumption and compare it with the budget
7. If the organisation does not allow usage-billed agents: record in writing the decision not to create a policy
--- Functional test documented by Microsoft ---
Have an eligible user submit a prompt to the 'Learning Coach' agent (around 12 credits), then check that the consumption appears in the Copilot Credits report
items.Expected: If the organisation allows Copilot Chat or SharePoint agents: a billing policy exists, it is attached to an Azure subscription in the same tenant and to a resource group, it is connected to the service under Copilot > Billing and usage > Usage-based services, and a budget with notifications and a named recipient is defined. Otherwise, the absence of a policy is a documented decision.
items.Verification: Manual verification: https://admin.cloud.microsoft > Copilot > Billing and usage > 'Billing policies' and 'Usage-based services' tabs. No Microsoft Graph endpoint and no public cmdlet exposes this configuration.

items.Requirement: Block self-service purchase of Microsoft 365 Copilot licences
items.Rationale: The framework checks the purchase, assignment and clean-up of Copilot licences (requirements 2 to 5, 14, 15) but not the door through which licences appear without going through IT: self-service purchase. The Copilot scenario management page exposes this setting explicitly under Copilot > Settings > User access, with three possible values: allow, allow trials only, do not allow. A user who buys their own Copilot licence with a credit card creates a licence that IT never sees coming: it escapes the group-based assignment enforced by requirement 4, hence the conditional access policies targeting the Copilot group, hence the access review and the budget tracking. The employee gets Copilot access to their work data without a single governance requirement of this framework applying to them, and the invoice arrives through a channel separate from the enterprise agreement. This setting is readable read-only through the MSCommerce module, which makes it an automatable check at no cost, provided the product identifier is read from the command output rather than hard-coded. No Microsoft Graph endpoint exposes this setting: the MSCommerce module, connected with a Billing Administrator or Global Administrator role, remains the only source.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Billing > Your products > 'Self-service purchase' tab: check the state of the Microsoft 365 Copilot product
3. Set the product to 'Do not allow' to block both the purchase and the trial
--- OR through PowerShell (read) ---
1. Install-Module -Name MSCommerce
2. Import-Module MSCommerce ; Connect-MSCommerce (Billing Administrator or Global Administrator account)
3. Get-MSCommerceProductPolicies -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase | Where-Object { $_.ProductName -like '*Copilot*' }
--- OR through PowerShell (remediation) ---
4. Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductId read at step 3> -Enabled $false
5. Run step 3 again to confirm that the value is now 'Disabled'
items.Expected: The AllowSelfServicePurchase policy value is 'Disabled' for every Microsoft 365 Copilot product exposed by the tenant (or 'OnlyTrialsWithoutPaymentMethod' with a documented decision); no Copilot licence has been acquired outside the central purchase channel.
items.Verification: Import-Module MSCommerce ; Connect-MSCommerce ; Get-MSCommerceProductPolicies -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase | Where-Object { $_.ProductName -like '*Copilot*' } | Select-Object ProductName, ProductId, PolicyValue

items.Requirement: Keep a watch on message center announcements about Copilot changes that require action
items.Rationale: Copilot is the fastest-moving Microsoft 365 service: new workloads, changes to default behaviour, admin settings moved elsewhere, existing controls withdrawn. Those changes are announced only through the message center, often with an action deadline and a major-change marker. An organisation that does not watch those messages discovers the changes when a user raises a ticket, or worse when a governance setting it believed frozen has silently changed its default value: the compliance recorded at the last audit is then worth nothing. The service communications API makes it possible to automate that watch in version v1.0, with a dedicated permission, and to turn it into a measurable check: no Copilot message requiring action should remain untreated past its deadline. It is also the only reliable way to detect that the audit framework itself has become obsolete, because a check covers a setting that Microsoft has moved or removed. The handling state of a message (read, archived) belongs to the signed-in account and exists only in delegated mode: in application mode the engine sees the deadline without knowing whether it has been handled, which the evidence states explicitly. Finally, the watch requires a named recipient: without an owner identified in the message center preferences, the notifications are lost in a shared mailbox nobody reads.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Health > Message center
3. Filter on the 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' service and sort by action-required date
4. Handle every message requiring action before its deadline, then archive it to record that it was handled
5. Preferences (gear icon in the message center): turn on email notifications and name up to two recipients responsible for the Copilot watch
6. Review within 7 days any message flagged as a major change, and confirm that it does not alter the default value of a setting already audited
--- PowerShell verification ---
1. Connect-MgGraph -Scopes ServiceMessage.Read.All
2. Get-MgServiceAnnouncementMessage -All | Where-Object { $_.Services -contains 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' -or $_.Title -like '*Copilot*' } | Select-Object Id, Title, ActionRequiredByDateTime, IsMajorChange, Severity
items.Expected: 0 message center posts about Copilot whose action-required date has passed without recorded handling; every Copilot post flagged as a major change reviewed within 7 days; a named recipient for that watch in the message center preferences.
items.Verification: Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/serviceAnnouncement/messages?\$filter=services/any(s:s eq 'Microsoft 365 Copilot')" ; use actionRequiredByDateTime, isMajorChange, severity, category and services

items.Requirement: Copilot Studio agents at risk: 'None' authentication, maker-provided connections, creators outside the approved scope
items.Rationale: Copilot Studio lets a maker publish an agent with the authentication mode set to 'None': the agent then answers any caller, with no identification, while keeping the access to the knowledge sources and connectors its creator configured. Published on a reachable channel (website, Direct Line, anonymous Teams), such an agent turns an internal document base into an open question-and-answer service, which is the most direct leak scenario in the whole agent domain. It leaves no trace on the SharePoint permission side, because the content is queried with the creator's identity rather than the caller's, so no sharing report will ever surface it. The same mechanism applies to connections: when a broadly shared agent uses connections provided by its maker, the permissions of a senior profile are extended to the entire organisation and the Microsoft 365 permission model, on which the whole security of Copilot rests, is bypassed. The third facet, creators outside the authorised maker group, reveals the agents built outside any approval process and therefore never reviewed by security. The Copilot Studio inventory now exposes the authentication mode, the publication channels and the owner of each agent, which makes these three assertions measurable from a single inventory probe. Without this check, an organisation can have locked down its entire Microsoft 365 tenant and still expose its internal documents through an agent published in three clicks by a business user.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Agents
3. Sort on the Authentication column and note every 'None' value
4. For each agent concerned: open https://copilotstudio.microsoft.com and select the agent
5. Settings > Security > Authentication: switch to 'Authenticate with Microsoft'
6. Publish the agent to apply the change (the authentication mode only takes effect after republishing)
7. Channels tab: close any remaining anonymous channel (demo website, Direct Line without a token)
8. Settings > Security > Connections: for a broadly shared agent, prefer 'Connections provided by end user' over the maker's connections
9. admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com > Settings > Features: check the security group allowed to create agents
--- Script verification ---
1. Add-PowerAppsAccount (Power Platform Administrator role)
2. Query the Power Platform inventory: resourcequery/resources/query, TableName = PowerPlatformResources, type == microsoft.copilotstudio/agents
3. Project properties.displayName, properties.authentication, properties.channels and properties.ownerId
items.Expected: 0 agent with properties.authentication = 'None'; every published Copilot Studio agent has properties.authentication = 'Microsoft Entra' (or 'Generic OAuth 2.0' with a documented justification); no broadly shared agent uses maker-provided connections; every agent creator belongs to the authorised maker group.
items.Verification: Add-PowerAppsAccount ; Copilot Studio agent inventory (resourcequery API or the inventory cmdlet of the Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell module): read properties.authentication, properties.channels and properties.ownerId. Target: 0 agent with authentication = None.

items.Requirement: Power Platform data policy governing the connectors and MCP servers available to agents
items.Rationale: Copilot Studio agents can call Power Platform connectors and, now, third-party MCP servers as tools. Without a Power Platform data policy, a maker can wire an agent fed with Microsoft 365 data to a consumer storage connector, a social network or an unaudited external MCP server in a matter of minutes: the data then leaves the compliance perimeter without ever passing through the Microsoft Purview DLP policies, which do not cover that path. Microsoft explicitly documents that blocking a Power Platform connector also blocks the tools of the MCP servers depending on it, and that only advanced connector policies can block a whole MCP server, since tool-by-tool blocking does not exist. Data policies are evaluated in real time: the maker sees the error at design time rather than after go-live, which makes this a cheap guardrail to operate. The default environment deserves particular attention, because it is the one where any user can publish without asking for any approval, and it is also the one organisations most often leave outside every policy. Without that boundary, the organisation has no technical means of preventing exfiltration: the only remaining barrier is the goodwill of the makers, and the incident will only become visible after the fact, in the logs of the third-party service. This is the single technical border between an enterprise agent and the internet of connectors, and the checklist carried no requirement on it until now.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com
2. Left-hand menu: Policies > Data policies
3. Check that at least one policy is active and covers the default environment
4. If no policy exists: New policy, then name the policy
5. 'Prebuilt connectors' tab: classify every connector as Business, Non-Business or Blocked
6. Put consumer connectors and unapproved MCP servers in Blocked
7. 'Custom connectors' tab: apply the same classification
8. 'Scope' tab: choose 'Add all environments', or explicitly include the default environment
9. Save the policy
--- MCP servers ---
1. Left-hand menu: Policies > Advanced connector policies
2. Block the unapproved MCP servers: tool-by-tool blocking does not exist
--- Script verification ---
1. Add-PowerAppsAccount (Power Platform Administrator role)
2. Get-DlpPolicy | Select-Object displayName, environmentType
3. Get-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId <guid> -PolicyName <policy id>
items.Expected: At least one active Power Platform data policy covers the environments hosting agents, including the default environment, with an explicit connector classification (Business / Non-Business / Blocked) and unapproved MCP servers classified as Blocked.
items.Verification: Add-PowerAppsAccount ; Get-DlpPolicy | Select-Object displayName, environmentType, @{N='Blocked';E={($_.connectorGroups | Where-Object classification -eq 'Blocked').connectors.Count}} ; complement: Get-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations

items.Requirement: Entra agent identities: owner and sponsor, match with the agent registry, Conditional Access coverage
items.Rationale: An agent becomes orphaned as soon as its creator leaves the organisation, yet its identity stays active and keeps both its Microsoft Graph permissions and its connections. Microsoft explicitly classifies 'No owner assigned' and 'Shadow agent' (an agent with no registry entry, no owner or no Entra identity) as critical severity risks on the 'Agents at risk' card of the admin centre. The Microsoft Entra Agent ID model defines three accountability relationships, owner, sponsor and manager: the sponsor receives the access package expiration notifications and decides whether the agent is renewed or retired. With neither owner nor sponsor, nobody is notified, no access review can complete, and the agent keeps reaching the organisation's data indefinitely, including long after the person who built it has gone. Microsoft also documents that Conditional Access policies targeting 'All users' do not include agent accounts: an organisation convinced it covers all of its identities actually leaves its agents outside every access condition, with no MFA and no device or location constraint. This API is in preview and its property names are not stabilised, so the check is informative, stays out of the compliance rate, and declares itself not applicable rather than issuing a verdict on a moving API surface. The reference evidence remains the 'Agents without owners' card of the agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin centre, which must display 0.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Agents > All agents > Registry tab
3. Review the 'Agents without owners' card: the target is 0
4. Select each flagged agent > Owners: add an active human owner, then a sponsor
5. Reconcile the registry list with the agent identity inventory: any agent without an Entra identity is a shadow agent, to be regularised or retired
--- Conditional Access ---
1. Open https://entra.microsoft.com
2. Protection > Conditional Access > Policies
3. Check that at least one enabled policy targets agent identities: a policy targeting 'All users' does not include them
--- Script verification (preview capability) ---
1. GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity (AgentIdentity.Read.All scope, Agent ID Administrator role)
2. For each identity: GET .../servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity/<id>/owners then /sponsors
items.Expected: 0 agent identity with neither owner NOR sponsor; the 'Agents without owners' counter of the agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin centre is 0; every agent identity with accountEnabled = true has at least one active human owner; at least one Conditional Access policy explicitly targets agent identities.
items.Verification: Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method GET -Uri 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity?$expand=owners' (AgentIdentity.Read.All scope); then .../microsoft.graph.agentIdentity/<id>/sponsors. Preview API: if it does not answer, verify through admin.cloud.microsoft > Agents > Registry.

items.Requirement: Decide on Copilot access to open content and on its availability in the admin centres
items.Rationale: Two settings exposed by the Copilot policy settings API were covered by no requirement in the checklist. The first, 'Block Copilot Access to Open Content', decides whether Copilot may ground its answers on the file or page the user currently has open, outside the indexed boundary. Its stake is the mirror image of oversharing: Restricted Content Discovery, Restricted SharePoint Search and sensitivity labels act on discovery and on the index, never on a document already open on screen, as the Microsoft documentation states explicitly. In a sector where a workstation handles client or patient files displayed on screen, the decision must be taken and traced before the pilot opens, not discovered after an incident. The second, 'Copilot in Microsoft 365 admin centers', decides whether administrators may use Copilot inside the administration consoles themselves: this is a surface distinct from all the others, handled by highly privileged accounts that work on tenant configuration, roles and licences. Allowing Copilot in those consoles speeds up the work but means sensitive configuration details pass through prompts. Both settings are read through the same endpoint as web search and image generation: the cost of this additional check is nil.
items.HowTo:
1. Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft
2. Left-hand menu: Copilot > Settings
3. 'View all' tab
4. Open 'Block Copilot Access to Open Content' and decide according to the sensitivity of the content handled on screen
5. Open 'Copilot in Microsoft 365 admin centers' and decide for highly privileged accounts
6. Save, so that each decision is carried by a tenant-level policy and can therefore be evidenced
7. Document both decisions and their review date in the governance file
items.Expected: Both settings carry an explicit decision recorded in a tenant-level policy: microsoft.copilot.blockaccesstoopenfiles and microsoft.copilot.allowinadmincenters return a non-null value. A null value flags a decision that was never taken, to be settled before the pilot opens.
